content: @instructure/ui@11.7.4 just released and it includes security vulnerabilities, so we need to update, however it includes multiple other component changes since 11.7.3 and we need an upgrade strategy that includes updated the deprecation set, removing deprecated elements, updating the color/size/etc. normalization, and validating/remapping/updating the token map for new tokens / dangling refs / etc.  This should be a foundational, comprenensive update strategy for instructure/ui so that 11.7.5 and 11.8.0 can be somewhat automated, or surface points of manual intervention in a semi-automated way.  This should also be reusable so we can start marking version support and compatibility layers for consumers (i.e. Wordpress, Angular, Vitepress...)

content.content:
1	# Architecture overview
2	
3	pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then turns
4	that single model into many small, individually-publishable packages — plain CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus,
5	React/Vue/Svelte/Angular, Tailwind/Panda/PostCSS, native Swift/Kotlin/Compose/Flutter, WordPress,
6	Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the smallest package that fits, or the unified `pantoken` meta
7	package that re-exports them all.
8	
9	## The pipeline
10	
11	`@pantoken/core` (the transformer) resolves the Tokens Studio graph into a canonical,
12	`@property`-aligned `Token[]` IR — icons rolled in as `<image>` tokens. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors
13	that IR plus the raw JSON as static files. Every emitter (`css`, `icons`, `astro`, `rehype`,
14	`swift`, and the rest) consumes the vendored IR. The native path runs `core.toStyleDictionary()`
15	→ `@pantoken/sd-config` (Style Dictionary v5) → `@pantoken/swift` / `@pantoken/cli`.
16	
17	## The upstream-decoupling constraint (the load-bearing rule)
18	
19	`@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` is GitHub-only — no npm publish, no types. `@pantoken/core`
20	depends on it. So a package that depended on `core` would transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream
21	into every consumer's install. To prevent that:
22	
23	- Type contracts live in a zero-dependency **`@pantoken/model`**.
24	- Web and emitter packages depend on **`model` + `tokens`** (both upstream-free), **never on `core`**.
25	- `core` carries an ambient `declare module "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` shim, since the
26	  upstream ships no types.
27	
28	When you add a package, keep it off `core` unless it genuinely runs the transform. Reach for `model`
29	(types) and `tokens` (the vendored IR) instead.
30	
31	## Workspace layout — organized by how you consume each package
32	
33	The axis is consumption, not language. The rule of thumb: **import the output → `formats/`;
34	generate it into another ecosystem → `platforms/`.**
35	
36	| Bucket       | What lives here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
37	| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
38	| `packages/`  | Core machinery: `model` (types, zero-dep), `core` (transformer), `utils` (shared resolver + drift helpers), `plugin-kit` (the plugin factory), `cli`, and `pantoken` (the auto-generated meta package).                                                                  |
39	| `formats/`   | Importable npm serializations of the IR — `tokens`, `css`, `icons`, `dtcg`, `scss`, `less`, `stylus`, `icon-font`, and `components`. You `npm i` and import these.                                                                                                       |
40	| `platforms/` | Foreign-ecosystem source you _generate_ via the CLI and publish to that ecosystem's registry — `swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, `hugo`, `email`.                                                                    |
41	| `renderers/` | Integrations that produce UI — `web-components`, `react`/`vue`/`svelte`/`angular` wrappers, `react-markdown`, `rehype`, `astro`, `pendo`, and CSS-var bridges (`shadcn`, `bootstrap`, `docusaurus`, `vitepress`).                                                        |
42	| `bundlers/`  | Build-pipeline integrations — `vite`, `tailwind`, `postcss`, `next`, `webpack`, `panda`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |

# Architecture overview

pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then turns
that single model into many small, individually-publishable packages — plain CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus,
React/Vue/Svelte/Angular, Tailwind/Panda/PostCSS, native Swift/Kotlin/Compose/Flutter, WordPress,
Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the smallest package that fits, or the unified `pantoken` meta
package that re-exports them all.

## The pipeline

`@pantoken/core` (the transformer) resolves the Tokens Studio graph into a canonical,
`@property`-aligned `Token[]` IR — icons rolled in as `<image>` tokens. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors
that IR plus the raw JSON as static files. Every emitter (`css`, `icons`, `astro`, `rehype`,
`swift`, and the rest) consumes the vendored IR. The native path runs `core.toStyleDictionary()`
→ `@pantoken/sd-config` (Style Dictionary v5) → `@pantoken/swift` / `@pantoken/cli`.

## The upstream-decoupling constraint (the load-bearing rule)

`@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` is GitHub-only — no npm publish, no types. `@pantoken/core`
depends on it. So a package that depended on `core` would transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream
into every consumer's install. To prevent that:

- Type contracts live in a zero-dependency **`@pantoken/model`**.
- Web and emitter packages depend on **`model` + `tokens`** (both upstream-free), **never on `core`**.
- `core` carries an ambient `declare module "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` shim, since the
  upstream ships no types.

When you add a package, keep it off `core` unless it genuinely runs the transform. Reach for `model`
(types) and `tokens` (the vendored IR) instead.

## Workspace layout — organized by how you consume each package

The axis is consumption, not language. The rule of thumb: **import the output → `formats/`;
generate it into another ecosystem → `platforms/`.**

| Bucket       | What lives here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/`  | Core machinery: `model` (types, zero-dep), `core` (transformer), `utils` (shared resolver + drift helpers), `plugin-kit` (the plugin factory), `cli`, and `pantoken` (the auto-generated meta package).                                                                  |
| `formats/`   | Importable npm serializations of the IR — `tokens`, `css`, `icons`, `dtcg`, `scss`, `less`, `stylus`, `icon-font`, and `components`. You `npm i` and import these.                                                                                                       |
| `platforms/` | Foreign-ecosystem source you _generate_ via the CLI and publish to that ecosystem's registry — `swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, `hugo`, `email`.                                                                    |
| `renderers/` | Integrations that produce UI — `web-components`, `react`/`vue`/`svelte`/`angular` wrappers, `react-markdown`, `rehype`, `astro`, `pendo`, and CSS-var bridges (`shadcn`, `bootstrap`, `docusaurus`, `vitepress`).                                                        |
| `bundlers/`  | Build-pipeline integrations — `vite`, `tailwind`, `postcss`, `next`, `webpack`, `panda`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `design/`    | Design-tool assets — `figma` (Variables payload) and `swatches` (ASE/GPL/sketchpalette).                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `plugins/`   | Split by kind: `plugins/pantoken/*` are `PantokenPlugin`s (colors, focus/simple-icons/stacking/transition/visual-debug/primitives/logos); `plugins/postcss/*` are PostCSS plugins (prune-custom-props); `plugins/typedoc/*` and `plugins/vite/*` are docs/build tooling. |
| `tools/`     | Internal build tooling — `sd-config` (Style Dictionary, powers the native targets), `aggregate` (builds the meta package).                                                                                                                                               |
| `ai/`        | Consumer-facing agent assets (`@pantoken/ai`, `pantoken-ai`) — NOT for developing pantoken itself. It drops AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and editor rules into a _consumer_ repo.                                                                                                |

## The meta package

`pantoken` is auto-generated by `tools/aggregate`, which scans each package's
`"pantoken": { key, kind }` field. `kind` decides how a package joins the meta:

- `namespace` — eager barrel + subpath.
- `sideEffect` — barrel + an `/inject` subpath.
- `subpath` — subpath only, kept **out** of the eager barrel. Used for heavy React integrations (e.g.
  `react-markdown`, tailwind, panda) so `import "pantoken"` never pulls React or a build config.

`aggregate` only _writes_ the meta. When you remove a package from the meta, delete its orphaned
`packages/pantoken/src/<name>.ts` by hand — aggregate won't.

## Shared helpers

`@pantoken/utils` (deps: `model` + `arkregex`) holds the formerly copy-pasted resolver:
`makeResolver(base, {mode?, overrides?})` (a `var()` + `light-dark()` resolver) and `resolveTokens`,
plus the typed `VAR_RE`/`LIGHT_DARK_RE` regexes, `camelCase`, and `parseHexColor`. It also holds the
drift/validation harness — `unknownReferences(text, ir)` (bridge targets must be real tokens) and
`danglingReferences(css)` (self-containment: every `var()` has a definition in the same output) — plus
the generic token→class engines `colorUtilitiesCss` and `tokenUtilitiesCss`. `utils` must never import
from `components` (it sits below it). `checkPlugins` (the capability guard) lives in `plugin-kit`, not
`utils`.

## The gate

`pnpm run ready` must pass — a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`) that builds once, then fans out `vp check`,
test `-r`, CSS/JS lint, generated-output validation, and markdown lint concurrently. `pnpm run
check:publish` runs the publish gate (repository metadata + publint + attw). The same checks run on
every PR via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Generated artifacts (`platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
`platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, web-components `src/generated/`) are
gitignored and reproduced on build.

## Deliberate boundaries

- **canvas-ios and canvas-android get no dedicated targets** — both already self-generate from InstUI
  through their own Style Dictionary pipelines. pantoken's generic swift/android/compose cover the
  general native case; duplicating their in-repo scripts would drift.
- **Storybook is a renderer, not a design tool** — pantoken themes the Storybook _app_; it doesn't
  author design variables (that's Figma). The test is "theming the app" vs "providing
  design-authoring assets."
- **Go was declined** — no real Go UI consumer worth a target.

178	(Symbol.for("pantoken.plugin")) with capabilities inferred from its hooks. Also `extendPlugin(base,
179	overrides)` / `mergePlugin(...)` (compose plugins — chain same-stage hooks, merge CssContributions),

183	stage it lacks (passes through / skipped). Wired into the 3 IR/CSS transform consumers ONLY:

188	simple-icons migrated to `definePlugin` (dogfood). No c12/defu dep — c12 loads config FILES; this is
189	an in-code builder and composition = hook-fn chaining (defu can't merge functions).
190	`@pantoken/plugin-focus-outline` (dir `plugins/focus-outline`, key `focusOutline`; RENAMED from
191	`focus`/`plugin-focus` to match the InstUI focus-outline token namespace) emits an ANIMATED InstUI

193	colour+offset — zero-specificity). Exported fn `focusOutline()`, emitted props `--instui-focus-outline-*`.
194	Its defaults reference the shared focus-outline tokens but it RESOLVES them to concrete leaves against
195	`ctx.tokens` layered over the shipped IR of the chosen theme (`theme` option → else tokens-hook adopts
196	`ctx.theme` → else css-hook `rebrand`) so props are never dangling var() in native output and values
197	track upstream — no hardcoded fallbacks; hence it depends on `@pantoken/tokens` (via `byTheme`). Its
198	`css` hook self-defines `--instui-focus-outline-*` (skipping any the tokens hook already baked) so the
199	rules stand alone. Also has a `position: "append"|"prepend"` option (default append) + a ready-made
200	`--instui-focus-outline-transition` shorthand token. NOTE `:focus-visible` is a plain pseudo-class
201	(no `()`). Consumers: `renderers/astro` imports `focusOutline`; `renderers/pendo` consumes it too —
202	the plugin's ring is emitted (scoped to `._pendo-button, ._pendo-close-guide, ._pendo-text-link`) in a
203	LAST-declared `instui.focusOutline` layer (lowest !important priority — pendo adds !important to
204	everything, which REVERSES layer order so earliest layer wins; last = overridable baseline). pendo's
205	redundant per-component `:focus` outline rules + `--manual-light-focus-outline-*` tokens were removed;
206	the components with custom focus (select/textarea bg reset, radio/pagination sibling, card
207	focus-visible) keep their rules, rewired to the plugin's `--instui-focus-outline-*` tokens. (Unrelated: `formats/css` + `packages/core` tests use an inline fixture plugin
208	that happens to define `--instui-focus-color` — not this package.)
209	The `pantoken` meta package is auto-generated by `tools/aggregate` scanning each package's
210	`"pantoken": { key, kind }` field. `kind` is `namespace` (eager barrel + subpath), `sideEffect`
211	(barrel + `/inject` subpath), or `subpath` (subpath ONLY, kept out of the eager barrel — used for
212	heavy React integrations like instui-markdown so `import "pantoken"` never loads React). Design doc: [[../plans/i-find-myself-trying-adaptive-bachman]].
213	
214	Gate: `pnpm run ready` (build -r + vp check + test -r + markdown lint) passes; `pnpm run
215	check:publish` runs publint. Generated artifacts (`platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
216	`platforms/css/style.css`) are gitignored and reproduced on build.
217	
218	Rust: `@pantoken/rust` emits egui (`Color32`) or iced (`Color`) consts + f32 dims (bespoke, no SD);
219	CLI `generate rust --format egui|iced`. Alpha preserved (`from_rgba_unmultiplied` / iced `a`). Go
220	was declined (no real Go UI consumer; Fyne/Gio niche, Wails is web→CSS). Kotlin: NOT a separate
221	package — `@pantoken/compose` already emits Kotlin for modern Android; a plain-Kotlin target is only
222	worth it for non-Compose Kotlin Multiplatform (Android Views are covered by the XML resources).
223	
224	FUTURE GOALS (flagged, not yet done): (1) deepen native targets — the native emitters prove the
225	pipeline but only surface the flat color/dimension/icon set; make one (e.g. Compose) structured &
226	component-aware. (2) The deferred CI + typedoc + coverage-threshold rigor from the plan.
227	
228	`ai/` bucket (`@pantoken/ai`): consumer-facing agent assets (NOT for developing pantoken itself) —
229	AGENTS.md, llms.txt, Cursor/Copilot/Windsurf rules, a Claude Code bootstrap skill — plus an
230	installer + `pantoken-ai init` CLI that drops them into a consumer repo. Storybook is a renderer
231	(we theme the Storybook *app*), not a design tool (figma, which authors variables) — the test is
232	"theming the app" vs "providing design-authoring assets".

---
name: pantoken-architecture
description: "pantoken monorepo — purpose, layering, and the upstream-decoupling constraint"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8a0497fa-489b-45d2-847a-73f36df27207
---

pantoken (`~/Scripts/pantoken`) is a pnpm + vite-plus monorepo that turns Instructure design
tokens + `@instructure/ui-icons` into multi-platform, individually-publishable packages, unified
by an unscoped `pantoken` meta package.

Workspace is organized by semantic role (the axis is how you consume each package):
- `packages/` = core machinery: model, core, cli, pantoken (meta).
- `formats/` = importable npm serializations of the IR: tokens, css, icons, dtcg (W3C DTCG JSON),
  scss, less, stylus, icon-font. You `npm i` and import these. The three CSS-preprocessor formats
  (scss/less/stylus) are near-identical: each has `to-<x>.ts` (same resolveAll var()+light-dark
  flattener, single-mode), `index.ts` (ready-made `rebrand` export + default), a `scripts/generate.ts`
  that writes a static file after `vp pack` (`tokens.scss`/`.less`/`.styl`, all gitignored), vite
  `exports: false` (hand-managed so the static-file subpath survives), and `pantoken:{kind:namespace}`.
  Only the variable syntax differs: SCSS `$name: v;`, Less `@name: v;`, Stylus `name = v` (no
  semicolon). Icons are skipped in all three (icons belong in CSS).
- `platforms/` = foreign-ecosystem source you *generate* (not import) via the CLI and publish to
  that ecosystem's registry: swift (SPM), android (colors.xml/dimens.xml + icon VectorDrawables),
  compose (Kotlin), flutter (Dart), wordpress (theme.json); future drupal.
- `platforms/` also includes vanilla (Vanilla Forums Foundation `variables.json`). NOTE: Vanilla's
  "Foundation" is Vanilla's own theme engine (an enum layout value + a nested JSON variables asset
  at `PUT /themes/{id}/assets/variables.json`), NOT the get.foundation CSS framework — build it as a
  JSON variables mapping (`global.mainColors.*`, `titleBar.colors.*`, `button.primary.colors.*`).
- `renderers/` = integrations that produce UI: astro (Starlight), react-markdown, rehype,
  web-components (`<instui-icon>` + styled primitives), shadcn + bootstrap (CSS-var bridges; icons
  align via shared Lucide), and thin framework wrappers react (`<Icon>`/`useToken`/`TokenProvider`),
  vue (plugin), svelte (`icon` action), angular (`registerPantokenElements`) — all over
  web-components. Bridges (shadcn/bootstrap/vanilla) validate their mapped `--instui-*` names
  against the real IR in a test.
  Also react-native (StyleSheet-friendly resolved objects), storybook (ThemeVars theme).
  Static-site-generator theming: docusaurus (`@pantoken/docusaurus`, Infima `--ifm-*`→var(--instui-*))
  and vitepress (`@pantoken/vitepress`, `--vp-*`→var) are renderer CSS-var bridges like
  shadcn/bootstrap (static `custom.css`, aggregated namespace). jekyll (`platforms/jekyll`) + hugo
  (`platforms/hugo`) are PLATFORMS (no standard var contract) — they emit the token stylesheet as
  drop-in assets (`_sass/pantoken.scss`+`assets/css/pantoken.css` for jekyll; `assets/scss/_pantoken.scss`
  +`assets/css/pantoken.css` for hugo) reusing @pantoken/css+scss; CLI `generate jekyll|hugo`; NOT
  aggregated. DECISION: canvas-ios + canvas-android are NOT given dedicated targets — both already
  self-generate from InstUI via their own Style Dictionary pipelines (canvas-ios `scripts/instui/`
  bespoke SwiftUI formats; canvas-android `libs/instui/scripts/` SD v4 → Compose 3-layer, ~65
  component files). pantoken's generic swift/android/compose cover the general native case; duplicating
  their in-repo scripts would drift.
  pendo (`@pantoken/pendo`, key `pendo`, kind `subpath`): a REAL practical consumer — an
  Instructure-styled global stylesheet for Pendo guides. Component CSS (17 files, ~1263 lines:
  button/card/popover/alert/select/textarea/text/view/img/video/mask/pagination/radio-group/
  close-button + manual extras) ported VERBATIM from `@instructure/pendo-global-css`
  (`~/Scripts/pendo-styles`, branch `monorepo`, MIT). pantoken supplies the token layer via
  `toCss(byTheme(t), {scope:'[class*="instui"]'})` — the drop-in replacement for that repo's
  `instui-generate-css-tokens`→vendor/tokens.css (all referenced `--instui-component-*`/`--instui-icon-*`
  exist in pantoken IR; a var-ref coverage TEST asserts it). Assembled in `@layer` cascade order
  (layered !important beats Pendo's unlayered !important). CSS is inlined via a `scripts/embed.ts`
  codegen → `src/generated.ts` (gitignored) because rolldown `vp pack` can't resolve `?raw`.

  behavior. Token pruning was HOISTED to a shared global plugin `@pantoken/plugin-prune-custom-props`
  (`plugins/prune-custom-props`, key `pruneCustomProps`, namespace) — any renderer built on the full
  `@pantoken/css` layer but using a subset wants it (drops ~1800 unused icon data-URIs → 1.7MB→95KB).

  camelCased token keys (`colorBackgroundBrand`→`var(--instui-color-background-brand)`) for BOTH
  Emotion + styled-components (shared `props.theme` convention; also fits Stitches); `toStyledTheme(t,
  {resolve})` can bake concrete per-mode values. mui (`@pantoken/mui`) — maps resolved tokens to MUI
  `ThemeOptions` (palette primary/secondary/error/warning/info/success + background/text/divider +

  ships `lightTheme`/`darkTheme`; MUI is peer-only, return type is a local structural subset (zero
  runtime dep). DECISION: skipped Stitches (abandoned ~2022; covered by css-in-js). All three verified
  against real rebrand tokens. The 3 CSS-preprocessors + css-in-js + mui + panda all reuse the same
  inline resolveAll (var()+light-dark flattener) — duplicated per package, not shared (upstream-free).

  CSS inject), tailwind (preset), postcss (`@pantoken;` at-rule expands to the token stylesheet),
  next (`withPantoken` adds InstUI to `transpilePackages`), webpack (plugin emits pantoken.css),
  panda (`@pantoken/panda`: Panda CSS `definePreset` object — primitives→`tokens.colors`, themed
  light-dark tokens→`semanticTokens` with `{value:{base,_dark}}` (maps 1:1 to Panda's `_dark`
  condition), dimensions bucketed to spacing/sizes/radii/fontSizes/fontWeights/lineHeights/durations/
  shadows by value-type regex + name; keys strip `--instui-`. `kind: subpath` like tailwind — build
  config, kept out of the eager barrel).
- `platforms/` also: wordpress (theme.json), vanilla, drupal (`*.info.yml`/`*.libraries.yml` + css),
  email (concrete inline-friendly token maps). `@pantoken/core` icon-asset emitters now cover
  Android VectorDrawable, iOS `.xcassets` imageset (`toXcodeImageset`), and Flutter SVG assets +
  Dart manifest (`flutterIconManifest`); swift/android/flutter accept an `icons` option and the CLI
  a `--icons a,b` flag. CLI targets: swift, android, compose, flutter, wordpress, vanilla, drupal.

  swatches (`@pantoken/swatches`: flat colour palettes → Adobe ASE binary, GIMP `.gpl`, Sketch
  `.sketchpalette`; CLI `generate swatches --format ase|gpl|sketch`). KEY INSIGHT — design exports
  are two tiers: *interchange* (DTCG, Figma Variables) that tools *pull in*, vs *swatch/palette*
  files delivered *directly to a designer* to import (ASE/GPL/sketchpalette — colours only, a flat
  reduction of the tokens). Not aggregated into the meta (design-tool outputs).

  pipeline (pure JS, no native build): fill glyphs pass through; STROKE glyphs (Lucide) are outlined
  centreline→filled via `points-on-path` (flatten `d`→points) + `clipper-lib` (`ClipperOffset`,
  `jtRound`, `etClosedLine`/`etOpenRound`, offset = strokeWidth/2, SCALE=100) → `svgicons2svgfont`
  (`SVGIcons2SVGFontStream`, glyph = `Readable.from([svg])` with `.metadata={unicode,name}`) →
  `svg2ttf` → `ttf2woff2` (WASM; its build script is ignored, `allowBuilds: ttf2woff2: false`, still
  works). svgicons2svgfont v16 ships real types and has NO `log` option. CLI `generate icon-font
  --out dir [--icons a,b] [--class Name]`. NOT in the meta (heavy font toolchain kept out of
  `npm i pantoken`; install `@pantoken/icon-font` directly).
- `plugins/` = opt-in PantokenPlugin extensions: focus, simple-icons.
- `tools/` = internal build tooling: sd-config (Style Dictionary, powers swift/android/compose/
  flutter via its PLATFORMS map), aggregate.

`@pantoken/core` also emits native icon assets: `getIconSvgs` + `toVectorDrawable` (SVG → Android
VectorDrawable; handles path/line/circle/rect/polyline/polygon). `@pantoken/web-components` is
Node-safe: element classes are defined inside a guarded `register()`, so importing it during
SSR/build never touches `HTMLElement`. The small resolve-references helper is duplicated inline in
dtcg/scss/figma/wordpress (kept upstream-free rather than depending on core).

CORRECTION (user: "picking up some extra borders"): the stacked row is padding + the SINGLE bottom-border separator only (the row's existing `border-bottom` carries over) — NOT a full card box. Moved the modifier to the ROOT (`.instui-progress.-meter-color-{brand,info,success,warning,alert,danger}`, InstUI's `meterColor`) and paint the bar from the SEMANTIC `--instui-color-background-{brand,info,success,warning,error}` (distinct; alert→warning, danger→error). Added `-should-animate` (transition on `.bar`) + kept `.instui-progress-value`. (Progress-CIRCLE meter tokens ARE distinct — stroke-info/success/error — so circle colours were fine.) - **ProgressCircle:** restructured to a positioned container + `::before` conic ring + centred `.value` child; `@property --value {syntax:''}` registered (so the conic re-evaluates/animates); `-meter-color-*` naming; the demo Animate button works (was: no visible value; now updates `.value`). - **ToggleDetails FIXED (looked unstyled):** removed the native marker (`list-style:none` + `::-webkit-details-marker{display:none}`), added a rotating chevron `::before` (CHEVRON_RIGHT_ICON, `[open]`→rotate 90deg), `-variant-filled` (action-secondary summary), `-chevron-end` (iconPosition=end), sizes. **GOTCHA:** the modifier was first named `-icon-position-end` → it matched the generic `[class*="-icon-"]::before` glyph painter (undefined glyph → a solid square on the `

Tick now auto-contrasts: `oklch(from var(--…checkbox-background-checked-color) clamp(0,(0.62-l)*infinity,1) 0 0)` — same trick as the [[pantoken-architecture]] colors-plugin `onColor` util. - Radio dot sized `calc(100% - 2*inset)` collapsed to 0 (100% = border-reduced content box, and `checked-inset-md` is a 0.375rem @property initial-value). Fixed to `calc(var(--…control-size-md) - 2*var(--…checked-inset-md))`. **Native overlays: `` + popover + invoker commands (2026-07-07).** Modal/context-view now ride native platform primitives; checkbox `-variant-toggle` render bug also fixed this pass. - **Checkbox toggle bug:** the base control's `:not()` guard still named the pre-rename class — `const base = .${p}checkbox:not(.${p}checkbox.-toggle)` — but the variant is `-variant-toggle`. So the square base rules matched the toggle AND out-specified it (0,3,1 vs 0,2,1), rendering a checked square. Fixed the guard to `-variant-toggle`. Regression test asserts `:not(.instui-checkbox.-variant-toggle)` present and `:not(.instui-checkbox.-toggle)` absent. - **Modal → ``:** added `dialog.instui-modal { margin:auto; padding:0 }` + `dialog.instui-modal::backdrop { background: var(--instui-component-mask-background-color) }` + `.-blur::backdrop { backdrop-filter: blur(.5rem) }`. `.instui-modal` still works on a plain div. The class already out-specifies the UA popover border/padding, so no further reset. Anchor positioning to the trigger is consumer opt-in (Chromium); else it centres. - **Web Components (behavioral, NEW):** bespoke `` (renders a real `` once in shadow DOM — NOT the generic `wrapper()`, which repaints innerHTML and would reset dialog state; `open` attr → showModal()/close(); native close reflects back + fires a bubbling `close` event) and `` (host itself is `popover`, shadow resets `:host` + renders the class surface). Added to `ELEMENTS`; the "defines every element" test still matches. - **Commands:** NO `@pantoken/commands` plugin — the plugin contract (`PantokenPlugin` tokens/icons/css/rehype/native) only emits tokens+CSS, can't ship runtime JS. Built-in invoker commands (`command="show-modal"|"close"|"toggle-popover"`, `popovertarget`) cover open/close/toggle with zero JS; custom commands (alert dismiss, tab select) deferred to demo-local JS. - **Demos:** modal.html uses `command="show-modal"/"close"` + a feature-detected `showModal()` fallback for pre-2025 browsers; context-view.html uses `popovertarget`. Runner DOMPurify (`USE_PROFILES:{html,svg}`) passes ``/`popover`/`command`/`commandfor`/`popovertarget`. Browser-verified: modal opens as `:modal` top-layer with dimmed backdrop, closes via command; popover toggles + light-dismisses. Guide gained an "Overlays: dialog and popover" section; web-components README lists the two elements. 47 component tests, web-components tests, ready + check:publish all green. - **Modal `-size-fullscreen` fill fix:** a native `` defaults to `width: fit-content`, so the old `-size-fullscreen { max-width:none; margin:<40px> }` just content-sized the box (rendered small). Fixed to fill: `position: fixed; inset: var(--…full-screen-margin); width:auto; height:auto; max-width:none; max-height:none; margin:0` — overrides the dialog UA fit-content + `:modal` max-width cap so it fills the viewport minus the margin (works on a dialog or a plain positioned div). Browser-verified: viewport − 2×margin on both axes. Other sizes: sm 480 / md(default) 768 / lg 992 / auto fit-content(min 256). Demo shows all five via one trigger each. **Elevation moved into components; `@pantoken/plugin-elevation` DELETED (2026-07-07).** Enough components float (modal, alert, menu, demo card) that shadows are an intrinsic design attribute, not an opt-in plugin. `@pantoken/components` now owns elevation: `src/index.ts` exports `ELEVATION_NAMES`, `elevationDeclarations()` (`[name,value][]`), and `elevationCss({selector?})` (default `:root`). `componentsCss()` PREPENDS `elevationCss()`, so the `--instui-elevation-*` tokens lead every components.css and shadows resolve from components.css + a token sheet alone (browser-verified: modal `-has-shadow` alert both resolve with NO elevation.css). Why: they're the InstUI semantic layer, not raw token renderings. **Payoff:** the one real layering smell is gone — `@pantoken/plugin-primitives` imported `tokenUtilitiesCss` from the components FORMAT (a plugin reaching up); it now imports from `@pantoken/utils` (a lower shared tier), so its package.json dropped `@pantoken/components` → `@pantoken/utils`. utils now emits CSS (it didn't before) — accepted, since it already does `light-dark()` resolution + color math, so a generic string emitter fits. The two engine unit tests moved to `packages/utils/tests`. `@pantoken/utils` is NOT in the meta barrel (core tier, like `@pantoken/model`), so the engines are reachable via `@pantoken/utils` directly, no longer via `pantoken/components` — acceptable (they're low-level; the utility *classes* still ship via `@pantoken/components/utilities.css`). generate.ts imports the engines from utils; the `@demo self:{color,token}-utilities` tags moved WITH them (the runner's `self:` CSS set is fixed/global — includes utilities.css — so demos render from any package's API page). utilities.css + primitives.css byte-IDENTICAL after (pure relocation). Related decision (same session): stacking & transition stay opt-in plugins (no component consumes them; native overlays use the top layer + native CSS), NOT moved — the always-on-vs-opt-in test is "does a component's own CSS need it to render?" User chose: consolidate into components as a SEPARATE opt-in sheet. `formats/components/assets/fonts/` holds the woff2s; `scripts/fonts.ts` (`fontsCss(dir)`, ported from the plugin's generator — scans the woff2 dir, emits `@font-face` with `src: url("../assets/fonts/…")` + one `--instui-font-family-` :root var) is called by `generate.ts` to write `generated/fonts.css`; package.json ships `./fonts.css` export + `assets/fonts` in files. Split of concerns: base.css already APPLIES the font (`body{font-family:var(--instui-font-family-base)}`, system fallbacks) — `fonts.css` only LOADS the faces, so text degrades gracefully without it. Rewired: docs theme import (`@pantoken/plugin-font-families/fonts.css` → `@pantoken/components/fonts.css`; docs already deps components), docs/package.json + meta package.json dropped the plugin dep, meta re-aggregated (deleted orphan `packages/pantoken/src/fontFamilies.ts` by hand — aggregate only writes), guides (plugins.md/packages.md) updated. Browser-verified: 14 faces registered from the new fonts.css, body resolves to Atkinson, bold face LOADS (woff2 url resolves, no 404). 47 tests, ready + check:publish green. (hu guides + i18n-cache still reference the old plugin — pre-existing translation drift, deferred.) **Focus-outline moved into components' `base.css`; `@pantoken/plugin-focus-outline` DELETED (2026-07-07).** Same rationale as elevation ("so many things should have a focus outline out of the box") but it lands in **base.css**, not components.css — because it rings bare focusables (a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]) and NO component rule references its tokens, whereas elevation is consumed by component rules so it leads components.css. `@pantoken/components` src now exports `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, `focusOutlineDeclarations()` (`[name,value][]`), `focusOutlineRules(selector?)`, and `focusOutlineCss({selector?, tokenSelector?})`. `baseCss()` appends `focusOutlineCss()` (tokenSelector default `:where(:root)`). content.content: 1 # Engineering log 2 3 Hard-won fixes and gotchas from pantoken work. Each entry is symptom → root cause → the durable rule, 4 so future work doesn't re-learn the lesson. Version and PR numbers are deliberately left out; the 5 lesson is timeless. 6 7 ## Toolchain 8 9 ### oxfmt corrupts interpolated CSS-in-TS selectors 10 11 **Symptom** — After `vp fmt`/`vp check`, a component's compound selector silently changed meaning: 12 `${p}foo.-modifier` became `${p}foo .-modifier` (compound → descendant), and single-line rules 13 reflowed to multi-line. 14 15 **Root cause** — oxfmt (Prettier-based) treats `css` and `styled` tagged templates as 16 embedded CSS and reformats them. `embeddedLanguageFormatting: "off"` does **not** stop it — earlier 17 "it works" results were `vp` cache artifacts; verify with a clean cache. The tag name doesn't matter. 18 19 **Fix / rule** — Put a `// prettier-ignore` line immediately before each tagged template (before the 20 template for a direct arrow body, before `return` for a block body). oxfmt then leaves the template 21 verbatim and still formats the rest of the file. Don't use inline `/* prettier-ignore */` — it's 22 inconsistent for block bodies. When you add a record builder, tag it `css` and add 23 `// prettier-ignore` 24 or the next format pass rewrites its selectors. 25 26 ### Backticks inside a CSS comment terminate the template string 27 28 **Symptom** — A record's CSS template literal failed to compile after adding a `/* … */` comment. 29 30 **Root cause** — The `css` body is a JS template literal, so a backtick (or `${`) inside a CSS comment 31 closes the string early. 32 33 **Fix / rule** — Keep CSS-comment prose backtick-free and escape `${` inside the body. 34 35 ### `vp pack` doesn't resolve `?raw`; use `?inline` 36 37 **Symptom** — A published build failed with `[UNLOADABLE_DEPENDENCY] Could not load x.css?raw`, though 38 Vite dev and test worked. 39 40 **Root cause** — `vp pack` (rolldown) doesn't resolve Vite's `?raw` query; only the Vite dev/test path 41 does. 42 43 **Fix / rule** — Don't inline CSS via `?raw`. Vite+ now bundles `@tsdown/css`; import CSS with 44 `?inline` so pack, dev, and test share the same processed string contract. 45 46 ### A nested `vp` spawn dies under `vpr docs:dev` 47 48 **Symptom** — On a cache miss, a task spawned from inside the running VitePress process failed with 49 `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)`; cache-hit replays looked fine, so it 50 seemed intermittent. 51 52 **Root cause** — Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs under `vp`; a `vp run`/`vp pack` spawned from 53 **within** that process can't spawn. 54 55 **Fix / rule** — Spawn `node scripts/x.ts` directly from inside a `vp`-run process, never a nested `vp 56 run`. See `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`. 57 58 ### `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC` after a cssdoc bump 59 60 **Symptom** — Install or the docs dev-server startup failed with a missing catalog entry. 61 62 **Root cause** — pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*`, whose packages reference `catalog:` deps that 63 pantoken's own catalog must also carry. 64 65 **Fix / rule** — When cssdoc adds a catalog dependency, mirror it into pantoken's catalog. 66 67 ### Moving packages deeper stales the `.bin` shims 68 69 **Symptom** — After relocating packages one directory deeper, their `node_modules/.bin` relative shims 70 pointed at the wrong depth; a plain reinstall reported "up to date" and didn't relink. 71 72 **Fix / rule** — `rm -rf /*/node_modules && pnpm install` to force a relink. 73 74 ## Browser / bundling 75 76 ### A postcss-based value import kills the browser client 77 78 **Symptom** — On doc pages, all client JS died at app init with `createRequire is not a function` 79 (both light/dark theme toggles broke). 80 81 **Root cause** — `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` ship to the browser. A 82 **value** import of a postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` package made rolldown inject a `createRequire` / 83 `node:module` shim into the ESM build, which has no meaning in the browser. 84 85 **Fix / rule** — Keep `@cssdoc/*` value imports out of these packages' `src/`. Type-only imports are 86 fine (erased at build); value imports belong in build scripts and tests. Do doc-comment recovery with 87 a regex over the source, not a runtime `parseCssDocs` call. 88 89 ### VitePress runs Markdown through Vue 90 91 **Symptom** — A page module failed to compile, or custom elements rendered as unresolved Vue 92 components. 93 94 **Root cause** — VitePress compiles Markdown through Vue's SFC parser. It treats `` as an 95 unresolved component and tries to import a native ``'s file. 96 97 **Fix / rule** — Set `vue.template.compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (tag) => 98 tag.startsWith("instui-")` in `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`. In an `@example`, use an absolute/CDN/data 99 `src` or a custom-element `src` — avoid a native `` with a local path. The tag name doesn't matter. **Fix / rule** — Put a `// prettier-ignore` line immediately before each tagged template (before the template for a direct arrow body, before `return` for a block body). oxfmt then leaves the template verbatim and still formats the rest of the file. Don't use inline `/* prettier-ignore */` — it's inconsistent for block bodies. ## How pantoken ingests `@instructure/ui`

Important framing: pantoken does **not** depend on the umbrella `@instructure/ui` meta-package anywhere. It ingests two narrow upstream sources — `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` (tokens) and `@instructure/ui-icons` (glyphs) — plus a set of `@instructure/ui-*` React components used only by one renderer. Your "upgrade toward 11.7.4+" maps to the `^11.7.3` pins in the catalog.

### 1. Where `@instructure/*` is declared, and pinned versions

All versions flow through the pnpm **catalog** in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Package.json files reference `"catalog:"` rather than literal versions.

Catalog pins (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`):
- Line 26: `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens: github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens` — GitHub-only, **no semver pin** (this is why the tokens get vendored; see #4).
- Line 27: `@instructure/ui-icons: ^11.7.3`

Declaring package.json files:
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/package.json` lines 32-33 — `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` and `@instructure/ui-icons` as runtime `dependencies`. This is the ingestion package.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/tokens/package.json` line 37 — `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` as a **devDependency** (build-time only, for vendoring raw JSON + provenance).
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/renderers/react-markdown/package.json` lines 39-46 (deps as `catalog:`) and lines 63-70 (peerDeps as `*`) — the eight `@instructure/ui-*` React components. This is the only consumer of upstream InstUI React components.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/bundlers/next/src/index.ts` line 33 lists `@instructure/ui-icons` in `transpilePackages` (config string, not a dep).

### 2 & 4. The resolution entry point and the upstream-decoupling boundary

The single ingestion point is **`@pantoken/core`** (`packages/core`). Its description: "The pantoken transformer: resolves Instructure design tokens + ui-icons into the canonical @property-aligned token IR."

**Entry point — `buildTokens`:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/src/build.ts`
- Line 8: `import { themeTokens } from "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens";` — the **only** value-import of the upstream token package in the whole repo (aside from the vendoring script in #5).

  2. Layout (lines 112-116)
  3. Semantic colours, wrapping differing light/dark into `light-dark(...)` (lines 118-133)
  4. Components (lines 135-141)
  5. Icons rolled in via `collectIcons` (lines 143-150)
  6. Plugin icon + token hooks (lines 152-155)
- `THEME_SPECS` (lines 37-41) maps the three themes to upstream group/light/dark keys.

**Icon ingestion — `collectIcons`:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/src/icons.ts`

- `readCustomGlyphs` (lines 103-123) reads `svg/Custom/*.svg`; `readLucideGlyphs` (lines 125-172) reads the generated Lucide layer (`es/generated/lucide/index.js`) cross-referenced against `lucide-react`.

**Reference resolution:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/src/resolve.ts`
- `collectLeaves` (lines 60-88) flattens the Tokens Studio tree.
- `resolveValue` (lines 121-124) turns `{path.to.token}` refs into `var(--instui-…)`.
- `referenceToVarName` (lines 102-108) and `varName` (lines 139-142) build the `--instui-` custom-property names.
- `readModify` (lines 21-32) extracts Tokens Studio `$extensions."studio.tokens".modify` colour modifiers.

**Colour math:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/src/color.ts` — `applyModify` applies darken/lighten/alpha to concrete hex; reference-valued modifiers are preserved as `TokenModify` metadata for the native (Style Dictionary) lineage.

- `@pantoken/model` (`packages/model/src/index.ts`) is a **zero-dependency** package holding only the IR type contracts. - `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens`) vendors the resolved IR as **static JSON** so downstream packages never touch the GitHub-only upstream. Its `generate.ts` (see #5) doc: "This is what lets the published package ship with no dependency on the (GitHub-only) upstream."

Confirmed by grep: the only value-imports of `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` are `packages/core/src/build.ts:8` and `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts:10`. The only reader of `@instructure/ui-icons` is `packages/core/src/icons.ts`. Everything downstream (all `renderers/*`, `platforms/*`, other `formats/*`) reads from `@pantoken/tokens` or takes an IR array as input — e.g. `formats/css/scripts/generate.ts` → `formats/css/src/index.ts`, which consumes `@pantoken/tokens`. ---

### 3. The canonical model shape

Defined in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/model/src/index.ts`. The IR is a flat `Token[]`, each aligned to the CSS `@property` schema:

- `Token` (lines 54-65): `name` (e.g. `--instui-color-background-base`), `syntax` (`"<color>"` / `"<length>"` / `"<image>"` / `"*"`), `inherits: boolean`, `value` (concrete, a `var(...)` ref, or `light-dark(a, b)`), optional `themed?`, `refersTo?`, `meta?`.
- `TokenMeta` (lines 30-43): icon metadata (`kind: "icon"`, `style`, `viewBox`, `bidirectional`, `source`) plus a preserved colour `modify`.
- `TokenModify` (lines 18-27): `type: "darken" | "lighten" | "alpha" | "mix"`, `value`, `space?`, `color?`.
- `Theme` (line 15): `"rebrand" | "canvas" | "canvasHighContrast"`.
- Plugin contract (`PantokenPlugin`, lines 148-161) with per-stage hooks (`tokens`, `icons`, `css`, `rehype`, `native`) also lives here.

`core/src/model.ts` just re-exports these types from `@pantoken/model` so core files have a single type source.

**Token construction** happens in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/core/src/plugin.ts`:
- `defineToken` (lines 54-66) fills defaults: sniffs `syntax` from the value (`cssSyntaxForValue` / `isContextual` in `utils.ts`), sets `themed` for `light-dark(...)`, records `refersTo` for single-`var()` values.
- `dedupeByName` (lines 83-87), `runTokenPlugins` (lines 112-123), `runIconPlugins` (lines 161-177).

**Vendored form** (`formats/tokens/src/index.ts`): exports `tokens` (default = rebrand), `rebrandTokens`, `canvasTokens`, `canvasHighContrastTokens`, `themes`, and `byTheme(theme)` — each a `Token[]` loaded from `generated/<theme>.json`. Raw Tokens Studio JSON is at `@pantoken/tokens/raw`.

---

### 5. Scripts (resolve / ingest / sync / build:model / extract / generate)

No scripts literally named `resolve`, `ingest`, `sync`, `build:model`, or `extract`. The vendoring/ingestion is driven by **`generate`** scripts plus the `build`/`pack` step.

- **The canonical vendoring script:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (run via `formats/tokens/package.json` line 28: `"generate": "node scripts/generate.ts"`). It calls `buildTokens({ theme })` for all three themes, writes `generated/<theme>.json`, writes `raw.json` (verbatim `themeTokens`, line 26), and writes `meta.json` with upstream **provenance** — the resolved upstream version (lines 29-40). This is the ingest/extract step in practice.
- Root `package.json`: `"generate": "vp run -r build"` (line 8) and `"validate:generated"` (line 9) — recursive build across the workspace.
- Nearly every emitter package has `"generate": "node scripts/generate.ts"` (all `renderers/*`, most `formats/*`, `platforms/{wordpress,vanilla}`, several `plugins/pantoken/*`, `ai/pantoken-ai`). These read the already-vendored IR, not the upstream.
- `packages/core` and `packages/model` build via `"dev": "vp pack --watch"` / `vp check` (no generate).

---

### Upgrade blast-radius summary

To move `@instructure/*` from `^11.7.3` to `11.7.4+`:
1. Bump the catalog pins in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (lines 27, 54-61; the design-tokens entry line 26 is a GitHub ref, not semver).
2. Real ingestion risk is confined to `packages/core/src/build.ts` (token tree shape from `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`) and `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (filesystem layout of `@instructure/ui-icons`: `svg/Custom/`, `es/generated/lucide/index.js`, `icons.config.cjs`). These are the files that hardcode upstream structure.
3. Re-run `generate` in `formats/tokens` to re-vendor `generated/*.json` + provenance; everything downstream reads that vendored IR.
4. `renderers/react-markdown` is the only consumer of upstream `@instructure/ui-*` React components (separate concern from tokens/icons).
5. Provenance/version assertions to watch: `formats/tokens/tests/index.test.ts:26` and `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts:29-40`.

# Migration seed for the next Claude instance (LOCAL ONLY — do not commit)

Hand this to the new instance. It's the portable, personal layer that doesn't belong in the shared
repo: how the user works and a few hard behavioral rules. Everything else migrated into the repo —
start from `CLAUDE.md`, which maps the rest.

Kept short on purpose: the new plan has a tighter token budget, so seed only what can't be re-derived
from the repo.

## Who you're working with

- dwahl@instructure.com. pantoken is a personal repo (`github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken`) — it turns
  Instructure UI's design tokens and icons into multi-platform packages.
- Working style: decisive, security-forward, aiming at real production over shortcuts. Wants a
  credible scale-up path and faithful fidelity to the upstream (InstUI) rather than invented behavior.
- Decision style: one decision at a time, each with your explicit recommendation plus the tradeoff —
  then let them choose. Batch independent decisions into one question set (max ~4). Verify claims
  about third-party systems (upstream token names, browser support, a library's capability) before
  asserting — quote the source.
- Writing: active voice, contractions, plain language, Oxford comma. Never use these words —
  empowering, harnessing, unlocking, supercharging, transforming, game-changing, seamless, robust,
  leverage, synergy. (Org brand rules; fuller reference in the global `~/.claude/brand-voice-guidelines.md`.)

## Hard behavioral rules

1. **Never kill a process you didn't start.** "Port in use" is not "stale" — the user runs their own
   dev servers in other windows. Bind your own preview server to a distinct port with `--strictPort`.
   If a port you want is taken, pick another or ask — never `lsof … | kill` it.
2. **Use the `vp`/`vpr`/`vpx` CLIs — never raw pnpm/npm/yarn**, and package scripts must never shell
   out to `pnpm` internally (CI has no `pnpm` on PATH). Full rationale in
   `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`.
3. **Keep `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` runtime graphs Node-free** — they ship
   to the browser. Value imports of postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` are forbidden there; type-only is fine.

## Outstanding action items

- None open. The former cssdoc→pantoken migration item (switch the workspace to nested `../cssdoc`
  globs; retire the old `build-css-api.ts`) is **resolved**: pantoken now consumes `@cssdoc/*` from

1	# Release strategy and npm organization
2	
3	This document operationalizes pantoken releases using the existing `@pantoken` npm scope,
4	Changesets, and tag-driven GitHub Actions publishing.
5	
6	Release workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (package-tag driven).
7	
8	## Scope and goals
9	
10	- Keep the current `@pantoken/*` package names.
11	- Use automated semver and changelog generation.
12	- Publish via GitHub Actions on release tags.
13	- Support prerelease channels from day one.
14	
15	## npm organization model
16	
17	- Primary scope: `@pantoken`.
18	- Access: all packages published as `public`.
19	- Governance baseline:
20	  - enforce org-level 2FA for maintainers
21	  - require at least two owners
22	  - prefer trusted publishing (OIDC) from GitHub Actions
23	  - keep a break-glass token path documented and rotated
24	
25	## Versioning model
26	
27	- Tooling: Changesets (`.changeset/`).
28	- Bump model: independent package versions with internal dependency bumping set to `patch`.
29	- Changelog model:
30	  - per-package changelogs generated from changeset entries at versioning time
31	  - root `CHANGELOG.md` regenerated as an aggregate strict chronological feed (newest to oldest)
32	
33	## Release channels and tags
34	
35	Canonical package tag format: `@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`.
36	
37	Examples:
38	
39	- `@pantoken/components@v1.0.0`
40	- `@pantoken/components@v1.1.0-beta.0`
41	
42	Release scope for a package tag:
43	
44	- target package
45	- required workspace dependents resolved from internal `workspace:*` dependency edges
46	- `@pantoken/pantoken` auto-included when the release touches its exported dependency surface
47	
48	Dist-tag mapping in CI:
49	
50	- `-alpha.N` -> `alpha`
51	- `-beta.N` -> `beta`
52	- `-rc.N` -> `rc`
53	- any other prerelease suffix -> `next`
54	- stable tags -> `latest`
55	
56	## Standard release runbook
57	
58	1. Ensure branch health.
59	2. Run gates locally:
60	   - `pnpm run ready`
61	   - `pnpm run check:publish`
62	3. Generate version and changelog updates:
63	   - `pnpm run release:version`
64	4. Regenerate aggregate root changelog:
65	   - `vp run release:changelog:root`
66	
67	Bootstrap note:
68	
69	- For initial migration when historical package tags are missing, run
70	  `vp run release:changelog:root:seed` once to synthesize `v0.1.0` root entries from package
71	  changelogs.
72	
73	5. Commit those updates.
74	6. Create and push one or more package tags (`@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`).
75	7. CI computes the dependency-aware publish set and publishes with the resolved dist-tag.
76	8. Verify published versions in npm and install from a clean external project.
77	
78	## Prerelease runbook
79	
80	1. Enter prerelease mode:
81	   - `pnpm run release:pre:enter`
82	2. Create changesets for upcoming prerelease changes.
83	3. Version and tag prerelease (`@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z-beta.N`, for example).
84	4. CI publishes to prerelease dist-tag.
85	5. Exit prerelease mode when ready for stable:
86	   - `pnpm run release:pre:exit`
87	
88	## Rollback and incident response
89	
90	- Never unpublish stable releases except for policy/security emergencies.
91	- Prefer publishing a follow-up patch or applying npm deprecations.
92	- If a tag is wrong, publish a corrected version with a new tag; do not rewrite release history.
93	- If publish partially succeeds, re-run CI only after verifying already-published package set and
94	  adjusting versioning to avoid duplicate publish attempts.
95	
96	## First rollout checklist
97	
98	1. Validate trusted publishing setup on npm org and repo.
99	2. Run one prerelease cycle (`next`/`beta`) before first stable auto-publish.
100	3. Confirm dependency resolution and installability for representative packages and the
101	   `pantoken` meta package.
102	4. Confirm release notes generation and changelog quality.

- Use automated semver and changelog generation.
- Publish via GitHub Actions on release tags.
- Support prerelease channels from day one.

## npm organization model

- Primary scope: `@pantoken`.
- Access: all packages published as `public`.
- Governance baseline:
  - enforce org-level 2FA for maintainers
  - require at least two owners
  - prefer trusted publishing (OIDC) from GitHub Actions
  - keep a break-glass token path documented and rotated

## Versioning model

- Tooling: Changesets (`.changeset/`).
- Bump model: independent package versions with internal dependency bumping set to `patch`.
- Changelog model:
  - per-package changelogs generated from changeset entries at versioning time
  - root `CHANGELOG.md` regenerated as an aggregate strict chronological feed (newest to oldest)

## Release channels and tags

Canonical package tag format: `@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`.

Examples:

- `@pantoken/components@v1.0.0`
- `@pantoken/components@v1.1.0-beta.0`

Release scope for a package tag:

- target package
- required workspace dependents resolved from internal `workspace:*` dependency edges
- `@pantoken/pantoken` auto-included when the release touches its exported dependency surface

Dist-tag mapping in CI:

- `-alpha.N` -> `alpha`
- `-beta.N` -> `beta`
- `-rc.N` -> `rc`
- any other prerelease suffix -> `next`
- stable tags -> `latest`

## Standard release runbook

1. Ensure branch health.
2. Run gates locally:
   - `pnpm run ready`
   - `pnpm run check:publish`
3. Generate version and changelog updates:
   - `pnpm run release:version`
4. Regenerate aggregate root changelog:
   - `vp run release:changelog:root`

Bootstrap note:

- For initial migration when historical package tags are missing, run
  `vp run release:changelog:root:seed` once to synthesize `v0.1.0` root entries from package
  changelogs.

5. Commit those updates.
6. Create and push one or more package tags (`@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z`).
7. CI computes the dependency-aware publish set and publishes with the resolved dist-tag.
8. Verify published versions in npm and install from a clean external project.

## Prerelease runbook

1. Enter prerelease mode:
   - `pnpm run release:pre:enter`
2. Create changesets for upcoming prerelease changes.
3. Version and tag prerelease (`@pantoken/pkg@vX.Y.Z-beta.N`, for example).
4. CI publishes to prerelease dist-tag.
5. Exit prerelease mode when ready for stable:
   - `pnpm run release:pre:exit`

## Rollback and incident response

- Never unpublish stable releases except for policy/security emergencies.
- Prefer publishing a follow-up patch or applying npm deprecations.
- If a tag is wrong, publish a corrected version with a new tag; do not rewrite release history.
- If publish partially succeeds, re-run CI only after verifying already-published package set and
  adjusting versioning to avoid duplicate publish attempts.

## First rollout checklist

1. Validate trusted publishing setup on npm org and repo.
2. Run one prerelease cycle (`next`/`beta`) before first stable auto-publish.
3. Confirm dependency resolution and installability for representative packages and the
   `pantoken` meta package.
4. Confirm release notes generation and changelog quality.

questions.question: Should this effort execute the actual 11.7.4 bump, or just build the reusable machinery?

options.label: Build machinery, then run it for 11.7.4
options.description: Build the drift/diff + deprecation + compat pipeline, then use it to perform the 11.7.4 upgrade as its inaugural run — goldens, changesets, and all. One cohesive effort; the 11.7.4 diff is the proof the machinery works.

options.label: Machinery only
options.description: Design and build the reusable pipeline but stop short of bumping pins / regenerating output. You review the tooling, then trigger the 11.7.4 run separately.

options.label: Security bump now, machinery later
options.description: Do the minimal 11.7.4 security bump immediately (bump the ^11.7.3 pins, reinstall, re-vendor), defer the full strategy to a follow-up.

questions.question: How should we pin the GitHub-only `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` so upgrades are reproducible and deliberate?

options.label: Pin to a commit SHA
options.description: github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#<sha>. Fully reproducible; upgrades become an explicit SHA bump that flows through the drift pipeline. Requires manually choosing the SHA each bump (that's the intended control point).

options.label: Pin to an upstream tag
options.description: Pin to a release tag/branch if upstream publishes them. Cleaner than a SHA but only works if the repo tags releases — I'd verify that first.

options.label: Keep it floating
options.description: Leave github: (default branch). Simplest, but non-reproducible: any reinstall can silently change resolved tokens. Keeps the current behavior.

questions.question: Drift detection needs a committed baseline to diff each upstream bump against — but the repo gitignores all generated artifacts. Which baseline?

options.label: Compact token manifest
options.description: Commit a small purpose-built snapshot: token name → value/syntax/refersTo (+ icon inventory), per theme. Small, review-friendly PR diffs; the intended drift surface without duplicating full sheets. A narrow, deliberate exception to the gitignore rule.

options.label: Full resolved IR goldens
options.description: Commit the full per-theme resolved IR JSON as golden files. Exact and complete, but large, noisy PR diffs and a bigger break from the gitignore convention.

options.label: Compare against published npm
options.description: No committed baseline; CI diffs the new build against the last-published @pantoken/tokens artifact. Keeps gitignore intact, but drift isn't visible in the PR diff and depends on npm availability.

questions.question: How formal should the consumer version-support / compatibility layer be?

options.label: Manifest + generated doc table
options.description: A machine-readable compatibility.json (upstream version/range ↔ pantoken version ↔ validated consumers: WordPress, Angular, Vitepress, wrappers), validated in CI, rendered into a human doc table. Reusable and enforceable.

options.label: Hand-maintained doc table

## Upstream-drift detection and diff/report tool — design

### Context reconciled
- The upstream pins live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `catalog:` — `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` (a GitHub pin, no semver) and `@instructure/ui-icons: ^11.7.3`. A "bump" is an edit there plus `vp install`.
- Provenance today (`formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` → `generated/meta.json`, surfaced as `provenance` from `@pantoken/tokens/raw`) records only `{upstream, upstreamVersion}` for design-tokens. It does not record the ui-icons version. That's a gap the tool needs closed.
- `@pantoken/tokens` already exposes the resolved IR for all three themes (`themes`, `byTheme`) after `build:all` runs. The diff tool should consume that built output (the single generation path) rather than re-calling `buildTokens`, exactly like `tools/validate-generated/index.ts` imports `{ tokens }` from `@pantoken/tokens`.

---

### 1. Baseline artifact — recommendation: (a) compact committed manifest

Store a small, human-diffable manifest committed at **`tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json`** — deliberately outside any `generated/` dir, so it sits fine with the `**/generated/` gitignore rule. It behaves like a lockfile: a committed source-of-truth that CI keeps honest.

Shape (per theme token entries carry concrete short values; icons carry a hash of the large data-URI):

```jsonc
{
  "provenance": { "designTokensVersion": "11.7.4", "uiIconsVersion": "11.7.4" },
  "themes": {
    "rebrand": {
      "--instui-color-background-brand": {
        "syntax": "<color>", "inherits": true,
        "value": "#0374B5",            // authored value (var/light-dark kept verbatim)
        "resolved": "#0374B5",         // makeResolver-expanded leaf, for normalization review
        "themed": false, "refersTo": "--instui-primitive-blue-45"
      }
    },
    "canvas": { /* … */ }, "canvasHighContrast": { /* … */ }
  },
  "icons": {
    "--instui-icon-arrow-left": {
      "source": "lucide", "style": "Custom", "viewBox": "0 0 24 24",
      "bidirectional": true, "svgHash": "sha256:9f3c…"   // hash of the data-URI value
    }
  }
}
```

Tradeoffs vs the other two options:
- **(a) compact manifest (recommended):** small (a few hundred KB, no fat SVG data-URIs), reviewable directly in the PR diff, works offline, no network in CI, diffs before the first npm publish. Cost: it's a derived artifact you must keep in sync (the CI gate below enforces that).
- **(b) full resolved IR goldens committed:** every icon token is a giant `url('data:image/svg+xml;utf8,…')` string, so three-theme goldens are multi-MB and churn noisily. It directly contradicts the "`generated/` is reproduced, not committed" convention. Rejected.
- **(c) no baseline / diff against last-published `@pantoken/tokens`:** zero repo footprint, but the published dist embeds the IR inside bundled JS (`dist/index.mjs`), not clean JSON, so you'd import a tarball to reconstruct it; needs network in CI, can't run offline or pre-first-publish, and the npm "latest" may not equal the branch's true previous state. Good as a secondary cross-check, not the primary baseline.

---

### 2. Diff engine — new package `tools/upstream-diff/`

Mirror `tools/validate-generated`'s layout: private package `@pantoken/upstream-diff`, `src/index.ts` as the pure, unit-tested library, and a thin `index.ts` runner (node script) that wires it to the live build. `vite.config.ts`/`tsconfig.json`/`package.json` copy the `validate-generated` pattern (`vp pack` not needed since private; scripts run via `node`).

Library signatures (`tools/upstream-diff/src/index.ts`):

```ts
import type { Theme, Token } from "@pantoken/model";

export interface TokenSnapshotEntry {
  syntax: string; inherits: boolean;
  value: string; resolved: string;
  themed?: boolean; refersTo?: string;
}
export interface IconSnapshotEntry {
  source?: "custom" | "lucide"; style?: string; viewBox?: string;
  bidirectional?: boolean; svgHash: string;
}
export interface Manifest {
  provenance: { designTokensVersion: string; uiIconsVersion: string };
  themes: Record<Theme, Record<string, TokenSnapshotEntry>>;
  icons: Record<string, IconSnapshotEntry>;
}

/** Build a manifest from the live built IR (reuses resolveTokens for `resolved`). */
export function buildManifest(input: {
  themes: Record<Theme, Token[]>;
  provenance: Manifest["provenance"];
}): Manifest;

export type ChangeKind =
  | "token-added" | "token-removed" | "token-value-changed"
  | "token-syntax-changed" | "token-ref-changed"
  | "icon-added" | "icon-removed" | "icon-renamed" | "icon-changed";

export type ValueCategory = "color" | "length" | "number" | "image" | "other";

export interface TokenChange {
  name: string; theme?: Theme; kind: ChangeKind;
  before?: TokenSnapshotEntry | IconSnapshotEntry;
  after?: TokenSnapshotEntry | IconSnapshotEntry;
  category?: ValueCategory;   // derived from syntax; routes color/size normalization review
  renamedTo?: string;         // icon rename (removed+added sharing an svgHash)
}

export interface RefDelta { pkg: string; file: string; introduced: string[] }

export interface UpstreamDiff {
  before: Manifest["provenance"];
  after: Manifest["provenance"];
  buckets: {
    addedTokens: TokenChange[];
    removedTokens: TokenChange[];   // deprecation candidates
    valueChanges: TokenChange[];    // normalization review (color/size/etc.)
    syntaxChanges: TokenChange[];   // @property syntax changes
    refChanges: TokenChange[];
    addedIcons: TokenChange[];
    removedIcons: TokenChange[];    // includes renames when renamedTo set
    changedIcons: TokenChange[];
  };
  danglingDelta: RefDelta[];        // new dangling refs the bump introduced
  unknownDelta: RefDelta[];         // new unknown bridge refs the bump introduced
  manualReview: TokenChange[];      // the subset needing human intervention
  summary: { total: number; byBucket: Record<string, number>; needsReview: boolean };
}

export function diffManifests(before: Manifest, after: Manifest): UpstreamDiff;

export function toJsonReport(diff: UpstreamDiff): string;      // machine-readable
export function toMarkdownReport(diff: UpstreamDiff): string;  // PR-comment / human summary
```

Classification rules:
- Token buckets computed **per theme** (a value can change in `canvas` but not `rebrand`). Compare authored `value` for `refChanges` (retargeted `var()`), and `resolved` for `valueChanges` — so a change deep in the primitive chain surfaces even when the semantic token's authored `var()` is untouched. `syntaxChanges` and `inherits` flips are their own bucket (they change the emitted `@property` registration).
- `category` from `syntax` (`<color>`→color, `<length>`→length, `<image>`→image, `<number>`→number) routes the normalization review.
- Icons: keyed by token name; a removed name whose `svgHash` matches an added name is reported once as `icon-renamed` (renamedTo set) rather than a remove+add pair.
- `manualReview` = removed tokens + color/size value changes + syntax/inherits changes + `themed` flips + any `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta` + removed/renamed icons that appear in the CLI default set or fixtures (e.g. `arrow-left`, `check-mark`, which `validate-generated` hard-codes).

The runner `tools/upstream-diff/index.ts`:
1. Imports `themes` from `@pantoken/tokens` and `provenance` from `@pantoken/tokens/raw`; reads the ui-icons version best-effort (same `require.resolve(... /package.json)` trick as `generate.ts`).
2. `buildManifest(...)` → current manifest.
3. Reads committed `baseline/manifest.json`, runs `diffManifests`.
4. Writes `toJsonReport`/`toMarkdownReport` to a **gitignored** `tools/upstream-diff/report/` dir (add `report/` — or reuse the `generated/` convention) and prints the Markdown to stdout.
5. Exit non-zero when drift exists but the baseline wasn't updated (see CI gate), so the manifest can never silently fall behind the pin.

A separate `bless` script (run by the maintainer, not in the gate) rewrites `baseline/manifest.json` from the current build to accept a reviewed bump.

---

### 3. vp-run + CI integration, and semi-automation

**Task DAG (`vite.config.ts` under `run.tasks`)** — add, mirroring `validate:generated:only`:

```
"upgrade:check": { command: "vp run @pantoken/upstream-diff#diff", dependsOn: ["build:all"] }
"upgrade:bless": { command: "vp run @pantoken/upstream-diff#bless", dependsOn: ["build:all"] }
```

**Root `package.json` scripts:** `"upgrade:check": "vp run upgrade:check"`, `"upgrade:bless": "vp run upgrade:bless"`.

**Do not add it to `ready:all`.** A hard gate on every PR would fail every time someone intentionally bumps upstream (baseline stale until blessed) and cost a diff on unrelated PRs. Instead:

- **New CI job `upstream-drift` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**, gated by a `dorny/paths-filter` on `pnpm-workspace.yaml` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` (same pattern as the existing `docs-changes` job). It restores the vp task cache, runs `vp run -r build`, then `vp run upgrade:check`. It (a) uploads `upstream-report.md`/`.json` as an artifact, (b) posts/updates a sticky PR comment with the Markdown summary, and (c) **fails only if drift is detected but `baseline/manifest.json` in the PR doesn't already match the new upstream** — forcing the manifest to be blessed in the same PR that bumps the pin. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps the committed baseline honest without penalizing normal PRs.

**Semi-automated future bumps (11.7.5 / 11.8.0):**
1. Bump the catalog pin, `vp install`.
2. `vp run upgrade:check` → read the classified Markdown report, act on `manualReview`.
3. `vp run upgrade:bless` → rewrite and commit the baseline; open the PR (report as the body).
   Optionally add a scheduled `.github/workflows/upstream-drift.yml` (weekly) that re-resolves the pins, and if `summary.total > 0` opens a Renovate-style PR with the freshly blessed manifest and the Markdown report as the body — a human then reviews the buckets.

---

### 4. Reuse of existing helpers (no reinvention)
- `resolveTokens(base, { mode })` / `makeResolver` (`packages/utils/src/index.ts`) — compute the `resolved` field for the value-change bucket, so primitive-chain changes surface at the semantic layer. Snapshot with `mode: "light"` and `mode: "dark"` to also catch `light-dark()` branch changes / `themed` flips.
- `danglingReferences(css)` and `unknownReferences(text, ir)` — run over the **same** `SELF_CONTAINED` and `BRIDGES` package/file lists `validate-generated` uses, on the new build, to populate `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta`. To avoid duplicating those arrays, extract them into a shared const (e.g. export from `tools/validate-generated` or a tiny shared module) and import from both. This makes upstream-diff *attribute and classify* reference breakage to the bump, where `validate-generated` only pass/fails.
- `provenance` from `@pantoken/tokens/raw` for `designTokensVersion`; extend `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`'s `meta.json` to also record `uiIconsVersion` (read the same way it reads the design-tokens version) so the manifest's `before`/`after` provenance is complete.
- `Token`/`TokenMeta` types from `@pantoken/model` (`meta.kind === "icon"` distinguishes the icon layer). No new IR types — the manifest is a projection of the existing IR.

---

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/tools/upstream-diff/src/index.ts` (new — the diff library + report renderers)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/tools/upstream-diff/index.ts` (new — runner wiring live `@pantoken/tokens` build to the committed baseline)

# Design: token deprecation ledger + compatibility manifest

## Grounding summary (what exists today)

- Vendored IR is written by `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` → `formats/tokens/generated/{rebrand,canvas,canvasHighContrast}.json` + `raw.json` + `meta.json` (`{upstream, upstreamVersion}`). `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens/src/index.ts`) just imports those JSON files and re-exports arrays. Exports are `"."` and `"./raw"` only; `meta.json` is not currently exported.
- `buildTokens` (`packages/core/src/build.ts`) runs plugin `tokens` hooks as its last step (step 6), and `defineToken` (`packages/core/src/plugin.ts:54`) auto-derives `syntax: "*"` + `refersTo` for a single `var(--instui-*)` value.
- `toCss` (`formats/css/src/to-css.ts:71`) routes any contextual token (a `var()`/`light-dark()` value) into the `:root` declarations block; concrete tokens become `@property`. So a `var()` forwarder token becomes a real CSS shim in every downstream format for free.
- Drift primitives live in `@pantoken/utils` (`packages/utils/src/index.ts`): `tokenNames`, `unknownReferences`, `danglingReferences`. `tools/validate-generated/index.ts` is the drift gate; its `GENERATOR_PKGS`, `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS`, `BRIDGES`, `SELF_CONTAINED` arrays already enumerate exactly which consumers are validated and by which check.
- Release uses a writer/gate pair convention: `sync:repository` writes, `gate:repository` verifies (`vite.config.ts:116-123`). `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset whenever a publishable package's shipped source changes — regenerating `generated/*.json` counts.
- The inline-alias philosophy in `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts` clones a canonical rule body under the alias name. At the token layer we can do better than a body-copy: a `var()` forwarder keeps theming/`light-dark()` flowing through automatically.

---

## Artifact 1 — token deprecation ledger

### File

`formats/tokens/deprecations.json` — committed, hand-authored (package root, beside `generated/`, not inside it since `generated/` is machine-written). It's the durable, reviewed policy record; the companion drift diff only *proposes* entries.

### Schema

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./deprecations.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "token": "--instui-color-background-brand-old", // removed/renamed upstream token
      "since": "1.0.0",                    // upstream version it disappeared in (== meta.upstreamVersion)
      "policy": "alias",                   // "alias" | "removed"
      "replacement": "--instui-color-background-brand",
      "note": "Renamed upstream; forwards to the canonical brand background."
    },
    {
      "token": "--instui-legacy-spacing-xxs",
      "since": "1.0.0",
      "policy": "removed",
      "replacement": "--instui-spacing-xx-small", // migration target only; no shim emitted
      "note": "Hard-removed upstream. Migrate to the canonical spacing token."
    }
  ]
}
```

Policy semantics, reusing the inline-alias philosophy at the token layer:
- `"alias"` → emit a compatibility-shim token into the IR: `define({ name: token, value: "var(<replacement>)", meta: { deprecated: {...} } })`. `defineToken` yields `syntax:"*"`, `refersTo: replacement`; `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration, so css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla all get the shim automatically. This is the token analog of `withAliases`, but via `var()` forwarding (theming flows through) instead of a body clone.
- `"removed"` → **not** emitted. Surfaces only as a migration note (docs + CHANGELOG). Any pantoken-authored output still referencing it is already caught by `unknownReferences` in `validate-generated`.

### `@pantoken/model` type additions (`packages/model/src/index.ts`)

Zero-dependency, types only — fits the package's role as the IR contract:

```ts
/** Policy for an upstream token that was removed or renamed. */
export type DeprecationPolicy = "alias" | "removed";

/** One entry in the token deprecation ledger. */
export interface DeprecationEntry {
  token: string;
  since: string;
  policy: DeprecationPolicy;
  replacement?: string;   // required for "alias"
  note?: string;
}

/** The committed ledger shape (formats/tokens/deprecations.json). */
export interface DeprecationLedger {
  version: number;
  entries: DeprecationEntry[];
}
```

And one field on the existing `TokenMeta` (line 29-43) so a shim token carries its provenance into the IR (visible to consumers, docs, and the gate):

```ts
/** Present on an emitted compatibility-shim token (policy "alias"). */
deprecated?: { replacement?: string; since?: string; note?: string };
```

### Production / wiring

- New plugin `plugins/pantoken/deprecations` exporting `deprecationShims(ledger: DeprecationLedger): PantokenPlugin`. Its `tokens` hook appends one forwarder per `alias` entry:

  ```ts
  tokens: ({ tokens, define }) => [
    ...tokens,
    ...ledger.entries
      .filter((e) => e.policy === "alias" && e.replacement)
      .map((e) => define({
        name: e.token,
        value: `var(${e.replacement})`,
        meta: { deprecated: { replacement: e.replacement, since: e.since, note: e.note } },
      })),
  ]
  ```

- Insert it in `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads: `buildTokens({ theme, plugins: [deprecationShims(ledger)] })`. No separate release wiring is then needed — shims ship with `@pantoken/tokens` and every downstream format.
- **Fed by the drift diff** (companion tool): it compares `tokenNames(previousIR)` vs `tokenNames(newIR)` after an upstream bump; disappeared names become candidate entries pre-filled with `since = new meta.upstreamVersion`. A human sets `policy` + `replacement`. New gate `gate:token-drift` fails if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed) — this is the forcing function.
- Optionally export the ledger from `@pantoken/tokens` (`"./deprecations"`) so tooling/docs can read it without a file path.
