## Artifact 2 — compatibility manifest

### File

`compatibility.json` at repo root (a repo-wide release fact, like a lockfile-adjacent manifest), rendered into a human page at `docs/compatibility.md`. It's a writer/gate pair, mirroring `sync:repository`/`gate:repository`.

### Schema

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./compatibility.schema.json",
  "generatedAt": "2026-07-24",
  "upstream": {
    // token source — governs the token IR; unpinned github, provenance from meta.json
    "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens": {
      "range": "github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens",
      "resolved": "1.0.0",
      "feeds": "token-ir"
    },
    // icon source — governs the icon layer
    "@instructure/ui-icons": { "range": "^11.7.3", "resolved": "11.7.4", "feeds": "icons" },
    // the eight ui-* React packages — govern renderers/react-markdown ONLY
    "@instructure/ui-view":  { "range": "^11.7.3", "resolved": "11.7.4", "feeds": "react-markdown" }
    // ...ui-heading, ui-text, ui-link, ui-list, ui-table, ui-img, ui-alerts
  },
  "consumers": {
    "platforms/wordpress":       { "package": "@pantoken/wordpress",  "validatedBy": ["generated", "reference-integrity"] },
    "renderers/angular":         { "package": "@pantoken/angular",    "validatedBy": ["finalized-css"] },
    "renderers/vitepress":       { "package": "@pantoken/vitepress",  "validatedBy": ["generated", "reference-integrity", "finalized-css"] },
    "renderers/react-markdown":  { "package": "@pantoken/react-markdown", "instui": "^11.7.3" }
  }
}
```

The two-tier `upstream` split matters: the github-only design-tokens line (unpinned, "1.0.0") feeds the token IR, while the `^11.7.x` ui-* line feeds only `renderers/react-markdown`. ### Generation + validation

- `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` (writer). Sources:
  - token-source `resolved` ← `formats/tokens/generated/meta.json`.
  - each ui-* `resolved` ← installed `node_modules/.../package.json` via `require.resolve` (same technique `generate.ts:31` already uses for provenance).
  - each `range` ← the `catalog` block in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

"gate:compatibility":  { "command": "node scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts",     "dependsOn": ["build:all"] },

- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/packages/model/src/index.ts` (add `DeprecationEntry`/`DeprecationLedger`, `TokenMeta.deprecated`)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/tools/validate-generated/index.ts` (export consumer arrays; drift-gate integration)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/vite.config.ts` (new `sync:/gate:compatibility`, `gate:token-drift` tasks in the DAG)
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` (confirms bump PRs stay covered; pattern reference for the new writer/gate scripts)

# Instructure UI upgrade strategy — a reusable, semi-automated pipeline (first run: 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0)

## Context

`@instructure/ui@11.7.4` shipped security fixes, so we need to update. But a bump also pulls in
token, color, size, deprecation, and icon changes, and today pantoken has no repeatable way to see
what changed or to force the manual-review points to the surface. This plan builds a **foundational,
reusable upgrade pipeline** — drift detection, a token deprecation ledger, and a consumer
compatibility manifest — then **runs it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade as its first pass**.
After this, 11.7.5 and 11.8.0 become: bump the pin, run one command, review a classified report, and
either accept or intervene. The same manifest lets us mark version support for consumers (WordPress,
Angular, Vitepress, and the framework wrappers).

## Verified current state (grounds every decision below)

- **pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package.** The upstream surface is exactly
  three tiers:
  - `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` — GitHub-only, feeds the **token IR**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/build.ts`. Currently `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens` with **no
    ref** (floating); the lockfile happens to sit on commit `0db8a86…` = **tag `v1.4.0`**. Latest is
    **`v1.5.0`** (`ae8f600…`).
  - `@instructure/ui-icons` — `^11.7.3`, feeds the **icon layer**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (reads the package off the filesystem).
  - Eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (`ui-heading`, `-text`, `-link`, `-list`, `-table`,
    `-view`, `-img`, `-alerts`) — `^11.7.3`, consumed **only by `renderers/react-markdown`**.
- All pins live in the `catalog:` block of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Everything downstream reads the
  vendored IR from `@pantoken/tokens` (`formats/tokens/generated/*.json`), never `@pantoken/core`.
- **Provenance is broken.** `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` records `upstreamVersion` by reading
  the upstream `package.json.version`, which is **stuck at `1.0.0` on `main` across every tag**. So
  `meta.json` says `1.0.0` while we're really on `v1.4.0`. Provenance must record the **pinned tag +
  resolved commit**, not `package.json.version`.
- **No golden/value baseline exists.** Drift checks today are self-containment only —
  `danglingReferences` / `unknownReferences` in `packages/utils/src/index.ts`, run by
  `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`. Nothing captures resolved token values to diff across upstream
  versions.
- **Deprecations exist only at the component-CSS-modifier level**, authored inline as
  `@modifier -alias — @deprecated {@link .-canonical}` and cloned by `formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts`.
  There is no token-level deprecation record.
- The task DAG is `run.tasks` in `vite.config.ts`; gates funnel through `ready:all` and `gate:publish`.
  `scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when a publishable
  package's shipped source changes (re-vendoring `generated/*.json` counts). CI is
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No Renovate/Dependabot.

## Locked decisions (from you)

1. **Build the machinery, then run it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade** as the inaugural pass.
2. **Pin the GitHub-only design-tokens to a tag** — verified viable (`v1.0.0`–`v1.5.0` exist; GitHub
   Releases from `v1.3.0`). Move to `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`.
3. **Compact committed token manifest** as the diff baseline (not full IR goldens, not npm-only).
4. **Machine-readable `compatibility.json` + generated doc table**, validated in CI.

## What we build

Everything reuses existing helpers (`resolveTokens`/`makeResolver`, `danglingReferences`,
`unknownReferences`, the provenance capture, the `validate-generated` package lists) rather than
reinventing. All new tasks follow the `dependsOn: ["build:all"]` convention so codegen runs once.

### A. Fix provenance + pin the token source

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog: change the design-tokens entry to
  `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`; bump `@instructure/ui-icons` and the eight
  `@instructure/ui-*` packages `^11.7.3` → `^11.7.4`.
- `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`: rewrite the provenance block to record
  `{ designTokens: { ref, commit }, uiIcons: { resolved } }` — read the design-tokens **ref from the
  catalog pin** and the **commit from `pnpm-lock.yaml`** (the tarball URL carries the sha); read
  `uiIcons` via the existing `require.resolve(... /package.json)` trick. Keep `package.json.version`
  only as an untrusted secondary field. Export `meta.json` from `@pantoken/tokens` (`"./meta"`) so
  tooling and docs can read provenance without a file path.

### B. Upstream-drift tool — the core of the pipeline

New private package **`tools/upstream-diff`** (`@pantoken/upstream-diff`), mirroring the layout and
task wiring of `tools/validate-generated`.

- **Baseline** (committed, compact, deliberate exception to the `generated/` gitignore):
  `tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json`. Per theme: `name → { syntax, inherits, value,
  resolved, themed?, refersTo? }`; icons: `name → { source, style, viewBox, bidirectional, svgHash }`
  (hash the fat data-URI, don't store it). Plus the `provenance` block from (A).
- **Library** `tools/upstream-diff/src/index.ts` (pure, unit-tested):
  - `buildManifest({ themes, provenance })` — projects the built IR; uses `resolveTokens` at
    `mode: "light"` and `"dark"` for the `resolved` field so a change deep in the primitive chain
    surfaces at the semantic layer, and `light-dark()` branch / `themed` flips are caught.
  - `diffManifests(before, after): UpstreamDiff` — classifies **per theme** into buckets that map
    1:1 to your requirements: `addedTokens`, `removedTokens` (deprecation candidates),
    `valueChanges` (with a `category` of `color | length | number | image | other` from `syntax`, to
    route the color/size normalization review), `syntaxChanges` (`@property` registration changes),
    `refChanges`, `addedIcons`, `removedIcons`/renames (a removed name whose `svgHash` matches an added
    name is reported once as a rename), `changedIcons`. Plus `danglingDelta` / `unknownDelta` (new
    reference breakage the bump introduced) and a `manualReview` subset.
  - `toJsonReport(diff)` and `toMarkdownReport(diff)`.
- **Runner** `tools/upstream-diff/index.ts` — imports `themes` from `@pantoken/tokens` and provenance
  from `@pantoken/tokens/meta`, builds the current manifest, diffs against the committed baseline,
  writes the JSON + Markdown report to a gitignored `report/` dir, prints the Markdown, and **exits
  non-zero when drift exists but the baseline wasn't updated in the same change**. A `--bless` mode
  rewrites `baseline/manifest.json` from the current build (maintainer action, never the gate).
- **Reuse, don't duplicate:** extract `validate-generated`'s `SELF_CONTAINED` / `BRIDGES` /
  `GENERATOR_PKGS` / `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` arrays into a shared const both tools import, so drift
  attribution and the existing gate can't fall out of sync.

### C. Token deprecation ledger — "updated deprecation set" + "removing deprecated elements"

- **`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`** (committed, hand-authored policy; the diff only *proposes*
  entries). Each entry: `{ token, since, policy: "alias" | "removed", replacement?, note? }`.
- **`packages/model/src/index.ts`**: add zero-dep types `DeprecationPolicy`, `DeprecationEntry`,
  `DeprecationLedger`, and a `deprecated?: { replacement?, since?, note? }` field on `TokenMeta`.
- **`plugins/pantoken/deprecations`** exporting `deprecationShims(ledger)`: a `PantokenPlugin` whose
  `tokens` hook appends one **`var()` forwarder** per `alias` entry (`value: "var(<replacement>)"`).
  `defineToken` derives `refersTo`, and `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration — so the shim flows
  into css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla for free, and inherits theming/`light-dark()`
  automatically (a deliberate improvement over the component-layer body-clone). Wire it into
  `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads.
- `"removed"` entries emit nothing — they render as migration notes in docs + the tokens CHANGELOG.
- **Deprecation lifecycle:** a shim is added at the bump that removed the upstream token, kept through
  the current minor line, and pruned at the next major. Reconcile the existing inline **component**
  aliases the same way during this pass — that's the "removing deprecated elements" step.
- **Forcing function:** the upstream-diff `removedTokens` bucket feeds `gate:token-drift`, which fails
  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

### D. Consumer compatibility manifest — "marking version support"

- **`compatibility.json`** at repo root, with a two-tier `upstream` block (design-tokens → token-ir;
  ui-icons → icons; the eight ui-* → react-markdown), each carrying `{ range, resolved, feeds }`, and
  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,
  `renderers/react-markdown`, plus the framework wrappers) with the `validatedBy` checks each already
  passes.
- **Writer/gate pair** (mirrors `sync:repository` / `gate:repository`):
  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared
  `validate-generated` arrays. `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` regenerates in memory and
  fails if the committed file is stale (and asserts provenance agrees).
- Render `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table at `docs/compatibility.md` inside the
  existing VitePress/TypeDoc docs build.

### E. CI + task wiring

- `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`: add `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless`
  (`@pantoken/upstream-diff#diff|bless`), `sync:compatibility` / `gate:compatibility`, and
  `gate:token-drift`. Root `package.json`: matching `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless` scripts.
- Add `gate:compatibility` and `gate:token-drift` to `ready:all` (and `gate:publish`). **Do not** add
  the full `upgrade:check` diff to `ready:all` — it would fail every intentional bump until blessed
  and cost a diff on unrelated PRs.
- New CI job **`upstream-drift`** in `ci.yml`, gated by a `paths-filter` on `pnpm-workspace.yaml` +
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` (same pattern as the existing docs job): restore the vp cache, build, run
  `upgrade:check`, upload the report artifact, post/update a sticky PR comment with the Markdown
  summary, and fail if drift is unblessed in the PR. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps
  the committed baseline honest.
- Existing `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when `generated/*.json` churns —
  no new wiring needed there.

### F. Execute the inaugural 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade

1. Apply the pin edits from (A); `vp install`.
2. `vp run -r build` to re-vendor; `vp run upgrade:check` to produce the first report.
3. **Bootstrap the baseline** by blessing the *pre-bump* state first if needed (build at the old pin,
   `--bless`), so the first real diff is meaningful — otherwise the first run just records v1.5.0 as
   the baseline with nothing to compare. (Decide during implementation: bless at `v1.4.0` then diff to
   `v1.5.0`, giving a true first drift report.)
4. Work the report: author `deprecations.json` entries for `removedTokens`; review `valueChanges`
   (color/size) against the normalization code (`build.ts` light-dark collapse, `color.ts` `applyModify`,
   `utils.ts` `cssSyntaxForValue`); confirm `addedTokens` land in the IR; resolve any
   `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta`.
5. `vp run upgrade:bless` to commit the v1.5.0 baseline; `vp run sync:compatibility` to write
   `compatibility.json`; regenerate `docs/compatibility.md`.
6. Verify `renderers/react-markdown` still builds/tests against the ui-* `^11.7.4` bump.
7. Add changesets; run the full gate (below).

## Critical files

- Pins/provenance: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`, `formats/tokens/src/index.ts` (add `./meta` export).
- Drift tool (new): `tools/upstream-diff/{src/index.ts, index.ts, baseline/manifest.json, package.json}`; shared lists refactored out of `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`.
- Deprecations: `formats/tokens/deprecations.json` (new), `packages/model/src/index.ts`, `plugins/pantoken/deprecations/` (new plugin), `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (wire the plugin).
- Compatibility: `compatibility.json` (new), `scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (new), `docs/compatibility.md` (generated).
- Wiring: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Reusability — the future-bump runbook (11.7.5, 11.8.0)

1. Bump the catalog pin (a new tag for design-tokens, or `^11.7.x` for the ui-* line); `vp install`.
2. `vp run upgrade:check` → read the classified Markdown report; act on `manualReview`.
3. Author `deprecations.json` entries for removed tokens (or the gate blocks you); review color/size
   `valueChanges`.
4. `vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility`; commit; open the PR (report as the body).
5. CI's `upstream-drift` job posts the summary and enforces the blessed baseline; changesets and the
   compatibility gate enforce the rest. Optionally add a scheduled weekly workflow that re-resolves the
   pins and opens a Renovate-style PR when `summary.total > 0`.

## Verification

- Unit: `tools/upstream-diff/src` tests (bucket classification, icon-rename detection, per-theme diff,
  category routing); a fixture ledger through `deprecationShims` asserting a `var()` shim token appears
  in the IR with `meta.deprecated`; `generate-compatibility` / `check-compatibility` round-trip.
- Integration: `vp run ready` (build, `vp check`, `test -r`, css/js lint, `validate:generated:only`,
  the new `gate:token-drift` + `gate:compatibility`, markdown lint) and `vp run check:publish` both
  green. `vp run upgrade:check` produces a non-empty v1.4.0→v1.5.0 report.
- Consumer smoke: build `platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`, and
  `renderers/react-markdown` at the new pins; confirm no new dangling/unknown refs and that
  react-markdown still renders against ui-* `^11.7.4`.
- CI: open the upgrade PR; confirm the `upstream-drift` job posts the sticky comment, uploads the
  report, and enforces the blessed baseline.

## Open risks / watch-items

- **Provenance can't trust `package.json.version`** (stuck at `1.0.0`); derive from the pin ref +
  lockfile commit. This is the single most error-prone spot.
- **Baseline bootstrapping** (step F3): the very first `upgrade:check` needs a pre-bump baseline to be
  meaningful.
- **`github:#tag` resolution** in pnpm produces a tarball-commit lockfile entry; confirm `vp install`
  pins deterministically and the CI paths-filter watches both `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the lockfile.
- **Node-free browser graphs:** keep the new tooling (`tools/upstream-diff`, release scripts) out of
  `@pantoken/components` / `@pantoken/web-components` runtime imports — they're build/CI only.

compatibility manifest — then **runs it to perform the 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade as its first pass**.

either accept or intervene. The same manifest lets us mark version support for consumers (WordPress,

- **pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package.** The upstream surface is exactly
  three tiers:
  - `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` — GitHub-only, feeds the **token IR**. Consumed only in
    `packages/core/src/build.ts`. Currently `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens` with **no
    ref** (floating); the lockfile happens to sit on commit `0db8a86…` = **tag `v1.4.0`**. Latest is

    `packages/core/src/icons.ts` (reads the package off the filesystem).

    `-view`, `-img`, `-alerts`) — `^11.7.3`, consumed **only by `renderers/react-markdown`**.

  the upstream `package.json.version`, which is **stuck at `1.0.0` on `main` across every tag**. So
  `meta.json` says `1.0.0` while we're really on `v1.4.0`. Provenance must record the **pinned tag +
  resolved commit**, not `package.json.version`.

  `danglingReferences` / `unknownReferences` in `packages/utils/src/index.ts`, run by

  package's shipped source changes (re-vendoring `generated/*.json` counts). CI is
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No Renovate/Dependabot.

2. **Pin the GitHub-only design-tokens to a tag** — verified viable (`v1.0.0`–`v1.5.0` exist; GitHub
   Releases from `v1.3.0`). Move to `github:instructure/instructure-design-tokens#v1.5.0`.
3. **Compact committed token manifest** as the diff baseline (not full IR goldens, not npm-only).

  `GENERATOR_PKGS` / `FINALIZED_CSS_PKGS` arrays into a shared const both tools import, so drift
  attribution and the existing gate can't fall out of sync.

  entries). Each entry: `{ token, since, policy: "alias" | "removed", replacement?, note? }`.

  `DeprecationLedger`, and a `deprecated?: { replacement?, since?, note? }` field on `TokenMeta`.

  `tokens` hook appends one **`var()` forwarder** per `alias` entry (`value: "var(<replacement>)"`).
  `defineToken` derives `refersTo`, and `toCss` emits it as a `:root` declaration — so the shim flows
  into css/scss/less/stylus/wordpress/vanilla for free, and inherits theming/`light-dark()`
  automatically (a deliberate improvement over the component-layer body-clone). Wire it into
  `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` so shims bake into the vendored JSON everyone reads.

  the current minor line, and pruned at the next major. Reconcile the existing inline **component**
  aliases the same way during this pass — that's the "removing deprecated elements" step.

  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,

  passes.

  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared

- **Forcing function:** the upstream-diff `removedTokens` bucket feeds `gate:token-drift`, which fails
  if a newly-disappeared upstream token has no `deprecations.json` entry (alias or removed).

### D. Consumer compatibility manifest — "marking version support"

- **`compatibility.json`** at repo root, with a two-tier `upstream` block (design-tokens → token-ir;
  ui-icons → icons; the eight ui-* → react-markdown), each carrying `{ range, resolved, feeds }`, and
  a `consumers` block (`platforms/wordpress`, `renderers/angular`, `renderers/vitepress`,
  `renderers/react-markdown`, plus the framework wrappers) with the `validatedBy` checks each already
  passes.
- **Writer/gate pair** (mirrors `sync:repository` / `gate:repository`):
  `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` sources `resolved` from provenance + installed
  `package.json`s, `range` from the catalog, and `consumers`/`validatedBy` from the shared
  `validate-generated` arrays. `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` regenerates in memory and
  fails if the committed file is stale (and asserts provenance agrees).
- Render `compatibility.json` into a support-matrix table at `docs/compatibility.md` inside the
  existing VitePress/TypeDoc docs build.

### E. CI + task wiring

- `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`: add `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless`
  (`@pantoken/upstream-diff#diff|bless`), `sync:compatibility` / `gate:compatibility`, and
  `gate:token-drift`. Root `package.json`: matching `upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless` scripts.
- Add `gate:compatibility` and `gate:token-drift` to `ready:all` (and `gate:publish`). **Do not** add
  the full `upgrade:check` diff to `ready:all` — it would fail every intentional bump until blessed
  and cost a diff on unrelated PRs.
- New CI job **`upstream-drift`** in `ci.yml`, gated by a `paths-filter` on `pnpm-workspace.yaml` +
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` (same pattern as the existing docs job): restore the vp cache, build, run
  `upgrade:check`, upload the report artifact, post/update a sticky PR comment with the Markdown
  summary, and fail if drift is unblessed in the PR. This is the lockfile-style invariant that keeps
  the committed baseline honest.
- Existing `check-changeset-coverage.ts` already forces a changeset when `generated/*.json` churns —
  no new wiring needed there.

### F. Execute the inaugural 11.7.4 / v1.5.0 upgrade

1. Apply the pin edits from (A); `vp install`.
2. `vp run -r build` to re-vendor; `vp run upgrade:check` to produce the first report.
3. **Bootstrap the baseline** by blessing the *pre-bump* state first if needed (build at the old pin,
   `--bless`), so the first real diff is meaningful — otherwise the first run just records v1.5.0 as
   the baseline with nothing to compare. (Decide during implementation: bless at `v1.4.0` then diff to
   `v1.5.0`, giving a true first drift report.)
4. Work the report: author `deprecations.json` entries for `removedTokens`; review `valueChanges`
   (color/size) against the normalization code (`build.ts` light-dark collapse, `color.ts` `applyModify`,
   `utils.ts` `cssSyntaxForValue`); confirm `addedTokens` land in the IR; resolve any
   `danglingDelta`/`unknownDelta`.
5. `vp run upgrade:bless` to commit the v1.5.0 baseline; `vp run sync:compatibility` to write
   `compatibility.json`; regenerate `docs/compatibility.md`.
6. Verify `renderers/react-markdown` still builds/tests against the ui-* `^11.7.4` bump.
7. Add changesets; run the full gate (below).

## Critical files

- Pins/provenance: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts`, `formats/tokens/src/index.ts` (add `./meta` export).
- Drift tool (new): `tools/upstream-diff/{src/index.ts, index.ts, baseline/manifest.json, package.json}`; shared lists refactored out of `tools/validate-generated/index.ts`.
- Deprecations: `formats/tokens/deprecations.json` (new), `packages/model/src/index.ts`, `plugins/pantoken/deprecations/` (new plugin), `formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` (wire the plugin).
- Compatibility: `compatibility.json` (new), `scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (new), `docs/compatibility.md` (generated).
- Wiring: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

1. Bump the catalog pin (a new tag for design-tokens, or `^11.7.x` for the ui-* line); `vp install`.
2. `vp run upgrade:check` → read the classified Markdown report; act on `manualReview`.
3. Author `deprecations.json` entries for removed tokens (or the gate blocks you); review color/size

4. `vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility`; commit; open the PR (report as the body).
5. CI's `upstream-drift` job posts the summary and enforces the blessed baseline; changesets and the

- **Provenance can't trust `package.json.version`** (stuck at `1.0.0`); derive from the pin ref +
  lockfile commit. This is the single most error-prone spot.

content.thinking:
I'm reviewing the plugin architecture and how the deprecations plugin fits in—it's simpler than I initially thought since it can bake shims directly into the tokens IR through the tokens hook rather than needing its own CSS sheet or generate step. Actually, I should keep the plugin out of meta aggregation by omitting the `pantoken` field entirely — the aggregate scan only picks up packages that have it, so this avoids the complexity of scanning and validating generated files. The plugin itself can still be published as a standalone package since it's just a build-time utility, and consumers get the baked shims for free through the vendored JSON in `@pantoken/tokens`.

So core imports from `@pantoken/plugin-kit`, which resolves via the package exports pointing to dist, but if plugin-kit has no build script it won't be in the vp run -r build pipeline. I'm wondering if vite-plus bundles workspace dependencies from source during packing, or if there's an implicit build happening somewhere. The key issue is that `formats/tokens` runs `generate` at build time, which imports `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations` at runtime. Node resolves this through the package exports pointing to dist, so if the plugin hasn't been built yet, the dist won't exist and generation fails. # @pantoken/tokens

The npm-published, semver'd home for Instructure design tokens. Two things ship here:

- **The resolved IR** (default export) — the canonical `@property`-aligned token list, with icons
  rolled in, ready to consume in JS/TS.
- **The raw Tokens Studio JSON** (`@pantoken/tokens/raw`) — the source, re-published verbatim, so
  you get npm + semver access without pinning the GitHub-only upstream package.

Both are vendored as static JSON at build time, so installing this package pulls no upstream
dependency.

## Install

```sh
npm i @pantoken/tokens
```

Also available as `pantoken/tokens`.

## Usage

```ts
import { tokens, byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens";

tokens; // rebrand theme IR: Token[]
byTheme("canvasHighContrast"); // another theme

import { raw, provenance } from "@pantoken/tokens/raw";
raw; // the Tokens Studio tree
provenance; // { upstream, upstreamVersion }
```

The themes are `rebrand` (default), `canvas`, and `canvasHighContrast`. The `rebrand` theme resolves
light and dark into `light-dark()` where they differ; `canvas` variants are single-mode.

## API

- **`tokens: Token[]`** — the `rebrand` theme IR (also the default export).
- **`rebrandTokens`, `canvasTokens`, `canvasHighContrastTokens: Token[]`** — each theme's IR.
- **`themes: Record<Theme, Token[]>`** — every theme's IR, keyed by name.
- **`byTheme(theme): Token[]`** — look up a theme's IR by name.
- **`Theme`, `Token`, `TokenMeta`, `TokenModify`** — the IR types (re-exported from `@pantoken/model`).
- **`./raw`** — the raw Tokens Studio JSON tree, plus `provenance` (the upstream package and version
  it was vendored from).

## Related

- Consumed by every format package (`@pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/scss`, `@pantoken/dtcg`, and the
  rest) as the source IR.

## License

MIT

# @pantoken/tokens

The npm-published, semver'd home for Instructure design tokens. Two things ship here:

- **The resolved IR** (default export) — the canonical `@property`-aligned token list, with icons
  rolled in, ready to consume in JS/TS.
- **The raw Tokens Studio JSON** (`@pantoken/tokens/raw`) — the source, re-published verbatim, so
  you get npm + semver access without pinning the GitHub-only upstream package.

Both are vendored as static JSON at build time, so installing this package pulls no upstream
dependency.

## Install

```sh
npm i @pantoken/tokens
```

Also available as `pantoken/tokens`.

## Usage

```ts
import { tokens, byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens";

tokens; // rebrand theme IR: Token[]
byTheme("canvasHighContrast"); // another theme

import { raw, provenance } from "@pantoken/tokens/raw";
raw; // the Tokens Studio tree
provenance; // { designTokens: { package, ref, commit }, uiIcons: { package, resolved } }
```

The themes are `rebrand` (default), `canvas`, and `canvasHighContrast`. The `rebrand` theme resolves
light and dark into `light-dark()` where they differ; `canvas` variants are single-mode.

## API

- **`tokens: Token[]`** — the `rebrand` theme IR (also the default export).
- **`rebrandTokens`, `canvasTokens`, `canvasHighContrastTokens: Token[]`** — each theme's IR.
- **`themes: Record<Theme, Token[]>`** — every theme's IR, keyed by name.
- **`byTheme(theme): Token[]`** — look up a theme's IR by name.
- **`Theme`, `Token`, `TokenMeta`, `TokenModify`** — the IR types (re-exported from `@pantoken/model`).
- **`./raw`** — the raw Tokens Studio JSON tree, plus `provenance` (the upstream package and version
  it was vendored from).

## Related

- Consumed by every format package (`@pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/scss`, `@pantoken/dtcg`, and the
  rest) as the source IR.

## License

MIT

Starting on the upstream-diff library design, I need to figure out the token snapshot structure. The key decision is how to store resolved values—I could include both light and dark resolved values for every token to make the manifest complete, though that would increase the size, or I could compute them on demand using resolveTokens per theme and mode. I'm leaning toward storing the authored value plus the resolved light and dark variants for simplicity, even if it means a larger manifest.

Looking at the numbers: roughly 4,600 tokens across 3 themes, with about 1,800 of those being icons (which I'll hash to keep compact). The non-icon tokens would be around 2,700 entries, each maybe 150 bytes, totaling roughly 1.5MB as committed JSON. That's chunky but still acceptable—it's much smaller than the full IR with uncompressed data-URIs, and diffs will only show changed lines. The trade-off is between true compactness and capturing resolved values to detect deep primitive-chain changes, but I think storing the resolved values is worth the extra size since that's what actually catches when a primitive deep in the chain shifts.

Actually, reconsidering: if I drop the resolved field and just store the authored value, syntax, refersTo, and themed flag, I get a much cleaner picture. When a primitive's hex value changes, that shows up directly in the primitive's own entry as a value change—no need to fan out to every dependent token. The diff becomes root-cause focused: report the primitive changed once, not every semantic token that references it. And for normalization review, the authored value of a color primitive is concrete hex (clearly a color), while a semantic token's authored value is a var() reference (contextual). So the meaningful changes surface exactly where they matter—at the primitives themselves.

For icon entries, I need to store source, style, viewBox, bidirectional, and a hash of the SVG data-URI. I'm using SHA-256 hashing via Node's crypto module, which is available in the test environment, so that works fine for deterministic hashing without adding external dependencies.

Defining the manifest structure... Comparing token maps across themes to identify added, removed, and modified tokens — distinguishing between reference changes (when a token's refersTo target shifts), value changes (when the actual value differs), and syntax changes (when syntax or inheritance rules differ). For icons, I need to handle them separately since they're theme-independent. For added and removed tokens, I'll treat them as theme-independent structural changes—if a token appears in any theme after but not before, it's added; if it was in any theme before but not after, it's removed. For value or syntax changes on tokens present in both before and after, I'll compare per theme and report a single entry per token name showing which themes experienced the change. Now I'm refining the approach: I'll use the rebrand theme to determine structural changes (added/removed token names), then for each theme compare the actual values, references, and syntax. Icons work similarly since they're stored once across all themes. I'm also planning to include provenance tracking in the report and format the output as both markdown with capped lists and JSON.

For the runner, I need to set up the CLI with import statements for themes and provenance metadata, then handle the baseline manifest—if it's missing in bless mode I create it, but in check mode I treat it as a first run and exit cleanly with a note. The command-line flags control the flow: `--bless` writes the baseline, while `--check` (the default) compares against it, generates a report in a gitignored directory, prints markdown output, and exits with a status code based on whether there's drift and whether the baseline matches the current provenance.

The exit logic hinges on comparing baseline provenance against current provenance—if they differ, the pin changed but the baseline wasn't re-blessed, so that's unblessed drift and the gate fails to force a bless in the same PR. If provenance is the same but the manifest differs, that means the resolver or core logic changed the output without a pin change, which also requires re-blessing the baseline, so that also fails.

So the rule is straightforward: if the current manifest doesn't match the baseline manifest, fail and show the diff; otherwise pass. This is the lockfile invariant, and `--bless` updates the baseline to match current.

A normal PR that doesn't touch upstream or core will have manifest equal to baseline and pass. A PR bumping the pin will have manifest differ from baseline, causing the `upgrade:check` gate to fail until they bless in the same PR. The question is whether this lightweight manifest-equality check belongs in `ready:all`—the plan said no because a full diff on every PR seemed expensive, but this check is actually cheap and functions as a proper drift gate.

Including a `gate:upstream` check in `ready:all` would enforce the invariant locally and fail any PR that bumps upstream until blessed, which is exactly the forcing function we want. The cost is minimal since the manifest build is already part of ready, and comparing to baseline is fast. I'll add this check to `ready:all` and keep the richer report generation available through `upgrade:check`—though they're really the same command.

There's a bootstrapping concern though: `ready:all` would fail until a baseline exists, so I'll create the baseline as part of this work. For the output directory, I'll use `generated/` inside upstream-diff so it's covered by the existing gitignore pattern rather than adding a new entry.

input.content:
# @pantoken/upstream-diff

The upstream-drift gate. It projects the built token IR (every theme, plus the icon set) into a
compact, committed manifest, then classifies what an Instructure UI bump changed against that
baseline — added, removed, retyped, and re-referenced tokens, and added, removed, renamed, or changed
icons — into review buckets, and flags the subset that needs a human.

```sh
vp run upgrade:check   # diff current build vs baseline; write the report; fail on unblessed drift
vp run upgrade:bless   # rewrite the baseline from the current build (accept a reviewed bump)
```

The baseline (`baseline/manifest.json`) is committed and behaves like a lockfile: the gate fails when
it doesn't match the current build, so a PR that bumps the upstream pin must bless the baseline in the
same change. That surfaces every token and icon delta in the PR diff and in the printed report
(`generated/report.md`, `report.json`).

Reference integrity (dangling / unknown `var()` refs) is gated separately by
`@pantoken/validate-generated`, so this tool stays focused on token and icon drift.

Both files are now tracked and passing. Moving on to Task 7, I need to wire these tasks into vite.config.ts, the root package.json, and CI. I'm adding several task definitions to vite.config.ts's run.tasks section: `upgrade:check` and `upgrade:bless` that run the upstream-diff commands with build:all as a dependency, and `sync:compatibility` which generates the compatibility metadata file, also depending on build:all.

Now I'm thinking through `gate:token-drift` — the mechanism to ensure removed tokens have deprecation entries. The tricky part is that once a removal is blessed, it becomes part of the baseline, so the diff shows nothing. The gate needs to run against the diff itself (baseline vs current) to catch uncovered removals before they're blessed, forcing maintainers to add the deprecations.json entries first.

The cleanest approach is to make `upgrade:bless` refuse to accept a bump if any removed tokens lack ledger coverage, preventing untracked removals from being committed.

So `upgrade:check` just verifies the baseline is current and reports what's changed, while `upgrade:bless` does the actual ledger validation—requiring entries for every removed token before allowing the new baseline to be written. This puts the enforcement exactly where a maintainer makes the decision to accept the change, and the baseline gate ensures bless happened before merging.

Someone could theoretically hand-edit the baseline to bypass ledger coverage, but the upstream-drift CI job and code review would catch that. Now I need to wire the ledger coverage check into the bless path of the upstream-diff runner, reading both the deprecations ledger and the diff between old and current baselines.

The runner will need to depend on @pantoken/plugin-deprecations to use its `ledgerCovers` helper, which keeps the logic consistent. I'll update the bless path to enforce coverage before accepting a bump.

Writing validation logic...

Now I'm thinking about whether `gate:token-drift` should be its own task in the build pipeline, or if I should fold it into the bless command with a `--check-ledger` mode that validates the deprecation ledger against any removed tokens.

The issue is that during a normal state where the baseline matches current, there are no removals to check, so the gate would just pass. But during a version bump with unblessed changes, `upgrade:check` already fails on baseline mismatch anyway. The only real edge case where `gate:token-drift` adds independent value is if someone manually edits deprecations.json to add removals without corresponding ledger entries — which is rare.

I'm leaning toward keeping it simple: fold the coverage check into bless and skip the separate `gate:token-drift` task, even though the original plan listed it. But there's still merit in a ready-time validation that checks whether every "alias" entry in deprecations.json actually points to a token that exists in the current IR.

Actually, the existing validation already handles this — if a maintainer writes an alias with a bogus replacement target, `generate.ts` bakes it into the CSS as `var(--bogus)`, and `validate-generated` catches that dangling reference. So the coverage check in bless is sufficient, and I can skip the separate gate.

I'm reconsidering whether `upgrade:check` should be in `ready:all`. The original plan excluded it to avoid failing on intentional bumps and adding cost to unrelated PRs, but the check is actually cheap since it reuses the build output. Including it would enforce the baseline invariant locally and force a bless step when upstream changes, which is desirable — and unrelated PRs would pass instantly since the baseline matches current. The cost is negligible, so I'm leaning toward including it despite what the plan said.

But the user approved the plan that explicitly kept it out of `ready:all`, so I should respect that decision and follow the approved approach: keep `upgrade:check` out of `ready:all` and gate the drift detection in a separate CI job with path filtering. Still, I want some local enforcement in `ready` to catch unblessed bumps when running `vp run ready`.

The plan was clear: add `gate:compatibility` to `ready:all`, keep `upgrade:check` out of `ready:all`, and handle the drift gate in CI. So I'll add `gate:compatibility` to `ready:all` since it's cheap and always-on, leave `gate:publish` as is, and move the full upgrade check to a dedicated CI job.

I also need to add a `sync:compatibility` writer task, then set up the `upstream-drift` job in CI with path filtering on the workspace and lock files. Let me check the CI structure to match the existing pattern.

That's the precise moment coverage matters. Let me first read `ci.yml` to match its paths-filter job pattern.

name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay
  # `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a cold rebuild.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

  typecheck:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Typecheck
        run: vp check

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Test all packages
        run: vp run -r test

  lint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Lint CSS
        run: vp run lint:css
      - name: Lint JS
        run: vp run lint:js
      - name: Validate generated output
        run: vp run validate:generated:only
      - name: Lint Markdown
        run: vp run lint:markdown

  publint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: Build and publint (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping publint."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run -r build
            vp run gate:publint
            exit $?
          fi
          # publint only inspects the scoped packages, so build just their dependency closure ("...").
          build_filters=(); check_filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do
            [[ -n "${p}" ]] || continue
            build_filters+=("-F" "${p}...")
            check_filters+=("-F" "${p}")
          done
          echo "publint scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp run "${build_filters[@]}" build
          vp exec "${check_filters[@]}" publint

  attw:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+

content.thinking:
So the deprecation lifecycle works like this: when upstream drops something in a patch release, I mark it deprecated but keep the shim in place until the next minor version lands upstream, then cut a consumer minor release to remove it.

The key is that the ledger needs to track both when something was deprecated (the upstream version that dropped it) and when it'll be removed (the next upstream minor), so I can auto-generate "deprecated in X, will be removed in Y" documentation. The policy stays "alias" during the deprecation window, then flips to "removed" once the upstream minor arrives.

The tricky part is that whether to emit the shim depends on the current upstream version — if we haven't hit the removal threshold yet, keep shimming; once we reach it, drop the shim. This means the deprecationShims plugin needs to know what version of the upstream we're currently at to decide dynamically whether each deprecated item should still be aliased or fully removed.

Actually, a cleaner approach: the ledger entry itself tracks the state transitions. When an upstream patch deprecates something, a maintainer records it with a target removal minor. The plugin then emits shims for all currently-active deprecations. Once we bump to that removal minor, the maintainer updates the ledger entry to mark it as removed (or deletes it entirely), and the plugin stops emitting the shim. This way the ledger is the source of truth that gets hand-curated at each version bump, rather than the plugin trying to infer state from version numbers. Defining the deprecation ledger structure... the ledger entry gets deleted when you reach that upstream minor, which triggers the consumer minor bump. So the policy really just collapses to "always emit a shim while the entry exists" — the `removeIn` field serves as both documentation and a signal for when to prune it.

Now there's the trickier case: what if a token gets dropped upstream and there's no sensible replacement to offer? The policy says keep supporting it until the next minor anyway. In that scenario, the shim could freeze the token's last-known value as a literal — so something like `--instui-component-badge-notification-z-index: 1` stays available even though the original token is gone.

So a shim becomes more flexible: it can either forward to a replacement token via `var()`, or it can hold a frozen literal value when there's no replacement. I'm redesigning the deprecation entry to support both cases — an optional `replacement` field for the forwarding case, or an optional `value` field for the frozen literal case. If neither exists, we can't create a shim, but the tooling could auto-capture the last-known value from the baseline when proposing the entry.

Defining the deprecation entry interface... When a drift report identifies removed tokens, the maintainer creates ledger entries specifying when they were deprecated and when they'll be removed, along with either a replacement token or a frozen value to maintain compatibility. The shims get baked into the IR so support continues, and documentation automatically pulls from the ledger to show the deprecation timeline. Once the next upstream version lands, the drift check would show the token is already gone since it was removed in the previous version.

But here's the catch: the shim re-adds the token to the IR, so the blessed baseline actually includes it. When bumping to the new upstream version, if the ledger entry stays, the shim keeps the token in the IR and no diff appears. To actually remove it at that point, the maintainer needs to delete the ledger entry, which removes the shim and lets the token drop from the IR—showing up as removed again in the diff. But now the coverage gate would flag it as a removed token without a ledger entry, which creates a conflict with the removal workflow.

I need to rethink the gate logic. The real driver here is that removal is a deliberate maintainer action at the `removeIn` boundary, so the tooling should distinguish between removals that are intentional deprecation closures versus accidental removals. At bump time, detect upstream removals and require ledger entries to keep support via shims. Then at the `removeIn` boundary, help the maintainer identify which tokens are actually ready to be removed.

I can add a check that lists ledger entries whose `removeIn` has been reached, signaling which deprecations are due for removal. The maintainer then deletes those entries and cuts a consumer minor. Since the shim re-adds the token to the IR, the baseline contains it as an intentional part of pantoken's output, so the drift diff treats shims as regular tokens.

When a maintainer removes a shim at a new version, the diff shows the token removed, but the coverage gate would incorrectly flag it as an uncovered upstream removal. I need to distinguish between actual upstream removals and intentional shim retirements. The cleanest approach is to make the gate require that every removed token either has a ledger entry or was a deprecation shim being intentionally retired.

The ledger becomes the single source of truth for the deprecation lifecycle. Each entry has a status that's either set by the maintainer or derived from comparing the current upstream version against the `removeIn` version. While the current version is below `removeIn`, the status is "deprecated" and the shim gets emitted. Once the current version reaches or exceeds `removeIn`, the shim stops being emitted automatically, and the entry is expected to be deleted as part of a consumer minor release. I've got the shims in place with the correct lifecycle metadata—the truncate shim properly forwards to the paragraph line-height variable to keep the existing CSS working, and the badge z-index is locked at 1. Now I need to rebuild the upstream-diff tool since both its library and index files changed, then run the drift report to see how those two removed tokens show up.

Actually, wait—by adding these as shims to the IR, those tokens aren't removed anymore; they exist as shimmed versions. So the `removedTokens` bucket should be empty for them. The truncate token had the same value in the baseline (the line-height variable) and still does as a shim, so there's no diff there. For badge z-index, both the baseline and shim have the integer value 1 with matching syntax, but now the shim carries the `deprecated: true` flag in the manifest—which my diff logic doesn't actually check since it only compares syntax, value, and references, not the deprecated metadata itself. So that metadata change won't show as a diff either.

This means after adding shims, the drift report against v1.4.0 no longer flags these tokens as removed—they appear preserved, which is exactly the point. The shim makes the upgrade non-breaking. The coverage gate sees them as not removed, so no coverage is needed. But there's a workflow question: how does the maintainer know to add the ledger entry if the shim hides the removal from the initial diff?

The answer is they add the shim *because* the initial diff (before shims) showed the removal. The flow is: bump upstream → tokens drop → upgrade:check shows removal → maintainer sees it → adds ledger entries → rebuild with shims → tokens reappear → upgrade:check shows no removal. In my case, I added the ledger entries and rebuilt before re-running upgrade:check, so the current build already has shims. Running upgrade:check now against v1.4.0 won't flag truncate and badge as removed, but the other changes (icons, badge-size, refs) still show.

The coverage gate actually works correctly as a forcing function: it computes removedTokens by diffing v1.4.0 vs the current build. Since shims preserve truncate and badge, they don't appear in removedTokens, so coverage passes. But this only works because I already added the shims—if a maintainer bumped and forgot the ledger entries, those tokens would show as removed and the gate would fail, forcing them to add the entries. Once shims are in place, the gate is satisfied. However, there's a subtle gap: what if a maintainer bumps, sees the removed tokens, but doesn't add ledger entries and just bl

... Actually, to hard-remove a token immediately without a shim, you'd add an entry with neither replacement nor value—this makes shimValue undefined so no shim emits, the token stays removed, and ledgerCovers returns true since the entry exists, letting coverage pass. But if removeIn is set to now or past, dueForRemoval flags it and bless fails, so you'd need to add removeIn at the next minor version. For the user's model, immediate removal isn't really an option—everything gets a deprecation window. When upstream drops a token, we always shim it (with a replacement or frozen value) until the next minor, so coverage always requires a shim entry with a value. The only actual removal happens when removeIn is reached and the maintainer deletes the entry.

The lifecycle works out: drop → shim entry with removeIn set to next minor (coverage satisfied, dueForRemoval not yet fired) → reach removeIn → dueForRemoval fires → bless blocked → maintainer deletes entry → token removed → coverage exempts it via wasShim (it was shimmed before) → bless succeeds. upstream Truncate v2 no longer sets line-height) and `--instui-component-badge-notification-z-index`

name: instui-upgrade-pipeline
description: The reusable Instructure UI upgrade pipeline — drift diff, token deprecation lifecycle, and consumer compatibility manifest
metadata:
  type: project
---

pantoken has a semi-automated pipeline for upgrading its upstream Instructure UI sources, built
2026-07-24 during the 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0 bump. See [[pantoken-architecture]].

**Upstream surface (verified):** pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package. Three
tiers, all pinned in the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog: `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`
(GitHub-only, now pinned to a **release tag** `#v1.5.0`, feeds the token IR via `packages/core/src/build.ts`);
`@instructure/ui-icons` (feeds icons via `packages/core/src/icons.ts`); and eight `@instructure/ui-*`
React packages (consumed ONLY by `renderers/react-markdown`). Ingestion blast radius = those two core files.

**Provenance gotcha:** the design-tokens repo's `package.json` version is STUCK at `1.0.0` across every
tag, so provenance must record the pinned tag + the lockfile commit, never `package.json.version`.
`formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts` writes `generated/meta.json` = `{designTokens:{ref,commit}, uiIcons:{resolved}}`,
exposed at `@pantoken/tokens/meta` (and re-exported from `./raw`).

**Drift gate — `tools/upstream-diff` (`@pantoken/upstream-diff`, private):** `lib.ts` projects the built
IR into a compact committed baseline `baseline/manifest.json` (per-theme token snapshots + hashed icon set;
~2MB — the "compact" form vs ~13MB full IR) and classifies a diff into buckets (added/removed/value/
syntax/ref token changes; added/removed/renamed/changed icons — rename = matching artwork hash). Runner
`index.ts`: `vp run upgrade:check` (fails on unblessed drift, writes `generated/report.{md,json}`),
`vp run upgrade:bless` (rewrites baseline). CI job `upstream-drift` in ci.yml is paths-filtered on
pnpm-workspace.yaml/pnpm-lock.yaml/formats-tokens/tools-upstream-diff. NOT in ready:all (would fire on
routine core-output changes). Reference-integrity stays gated by `validate-generated` (not duplicated here).

**Deprecation lifecycle — `plugins/pantoken/deprecations` (`@pantoken/plugin-deprecations`) + ledger
`formats/tokens/deprecations.json`:** when upstream drops a token, add a ledger entry
`{token, deprecatedIn, removeIn, replacement?|value?, note?}` (refs are `<tier>@<version>`, tier ∈
`ui`|`design-tokens`). `deprecationShims(ledger)` bakes a shim per entry into the vendored IR — a
`var(replacement)` forward OR a frozen last-known `value`. Kept working until `removeIn` upstream minor is
adopted, then the entry is RETIRED (shim dropped) and a consumer minor is cut. Enforced HARD in bless:
(1) dropping a real upstream token requires a ledger entry (coverage); a dropped token that was itself a
shim is exempt (retirement, not unhandled removal); (2) `dueForRemoval` — once current upstream ≥ removeIn,
bless fails until the entry is retired. Applied in generate.ts as a POST-build step (not `buildTokens({plugins})`)
to avoid the icons-stage "no icons hook" warning.

**Compatibility manifest — root `compatibility.json` + `docs/compatibility.md`:** writer/gate pair
`scripts/release/{generate,check}-compatibility.ts` (+ `compatibility.ts`), mirroring sync:/gate:repository.
Records the two upstream tiers (token-ir/icons vs instui-react), consumers (derived by scanning
renderers/* + platforms/* for `@instructure/*` deps — react-markdown is the sole instui-react consumer),
and the deprecation lifecycle table. `gate:compatibility` (parse-compare, formatting-agnostic) is in
ready:all; `sync:compatibility` regenerates. `docs/compatibility.md` is a top-level page — NOT scanned by
the locale parity/drift checks (those only cover docs/guide, docs/api, docs/index.md).

**Ingestion fix this bump:** ui-icons 11.7.4 moved onto lucide-react@1.23.0 whose ESM is `.mjs`
(was `.js` at 1.7.0). `icons.ts` `readEsmModule()` now tolerates both extensions.

**Future-bump runbook:** bump catalog pin → `vp install` → rebuild core+tokens → `vp run upgrade:check`
(read the classified report) → author deprecations.json entries for removed tokens (or bless refuses) →
`vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility` → changeset → PR (CI upstream-drift enforces the
blessed baseline).

content.text:
Everything is implemented, verified, and recorded. I did **not** commit — that's yours to trigger.

## What's built

A reusable, semi-automated Instructure UI upgrade pipeline, then run to perform the 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0 bump as its first pass.

**Reframe that drove it:** pantoken never depends on `@instructure/ui`. The real surface is three catalog-pinned tiers — design-tokens (GitHub, now pinned to tag `#v1.5.0`), ui-icons, and eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (only `react-markdown` uses them). The whole ingestion blast radius is two files in `@pantoken/core`.

- **Provenance fix** — [generate.ts](formats/tokens/scripts/generate.ts) now records the pinned tag + lockfile commit + ui-icons version (the design-tokens `package.json` version is stuck at `1.0.0` across every tag, so it's untrustworthy), exposed at a new [`@pantoken/tokens/meta`](formats/tokens/src/meta.ts).
- **Drift gate** — [`tools/upstream-diff`](tools/upstream-diff/lib.ts) projects the built IR into a committed [baseline manifest](tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json) and classifies every upstream change into buckets (added/removed/value/syntax/ref tokens; added/removed/**renamed**/changed icons). `vp run upgrade:check` fails on unblessed drift; `vp run upgrade:bless` accepts a reviewed bump. Paths-filtered CI job in [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml).
- **Deprecation lifecycle** — [`@pantoken/plugin-deprecations`](plugins/pantoken/deprecations/src/index.ts) + the [ledger](formats/tokens/deprecations.json). Each dropped token gets a shim (`var()` forward or frozen value) that ships until its `removeIn` upstream minor, tracked as `deprecatedIn`/`removeIn`. Bless **hard-fails** two ways: a dropped token needs a ledger entry, and a shim past its `removeIn` must be retired — enforcing your `0.1.4 (deprecated) → 0.2.0 (removed)` cadence.
- **Compatibility manifest** — [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) + generated [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md), a writer/gate pair mirroring `sync:/gate:repository`, auto-documenting the upstream tiers, consumers, and the deprecation table.

**Inaugural v1.4.0→v1.5.0 / 11.7.3→11.7.4 result:** 77 classified changes — 52 new icons, 1 renamed (`text-select`→`square-dashed-text`), `badge-size` `1.25rem→1rem`, 4 ref retargets, plus 2 dropped tokens now shimmed: `truncate-text-line-height` forwards to `--instui-line-height-paragraph-base` (verified upstream Truncate v2 drops line-height and inherits), and `badge-notification-z-index` frozen to `1`. Also fixed lucide-react `.js`→`.mjs` ingestion in [icons.ts](packages/core/src/icons.ts) (the bump broke it).

**Verification:** `vp run ready` and `vp run check:publish` both fully green (build, typecheck, all tests, css/js lint, validate-generated, compat gate, markdown, publint, attw). Changeset authored in [.changeset](.changeset/instui-11-7-4-upgrade-pipeline.md).

## A few considered deviations from the plan
- `gate:token-drift` folded into `upgrade:bless` (it's a no-op once blessed; the accept step is where coverage matters).
- Shared-lists refactor descoped — reference-integrity stays gated in `validate-generated`; compat consumers are derived by scanning the workspace instead.
- Root `package.json` scripts dropped (they collide with same-named `run.tasks`); use `vp run upgrade:check` / `upgrade:bless` / `sync:compatibility`.
- CI surfaces the report as an artifact + job log rather than a sticky PR comment (avoids the write-permission/fork surface).

## Your call before committing
The changeset bumps `tokens`/`model`/`plugin-deprecations` **minor** and `core` **patch** (dependents cascade to patch automatically). Your versioning model frames a deprecation-*introducing* bump as a patch step (`0.1.3→0.1.4`) — if you'd rather this be all-patch, adjust [the changeset](.changeset/instui-11-7-4-upgrade-pipeline.md). Optional polish I left out: wiring `compatibility.md` into the VitePress sidebar.

Want me to commit this to `feat/instui-upgrade-pipeline` and open a PR?

gh pr create --base main --head feat/instui-upgrade-pipeline \
  --title "Upgrade to Instructure UI 11.7.4 + a reusable upstream-upgrade pipeline" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Context

`@instructure/ui@11.7.4` shipped security fixes, so we needed to update — but a bump also pulls in token, colour, size, deprecation, and icon changes, and there was no repeatable way to see what changed or force the manual-review points to the surface. This builds a foundational, reusable upgrade pipeline, then runs it to perform the 11.7.4 / design-tokens v1.5.0 bump as its first pass.

Reframe that drove it: pantoken never depends on the `@instructure/ui` meta-package. The upstream surface is three catalog-pinned tiers — design-tokens (GitHub-only, now pinned to tag `#v1.5.0`), `@instructure/ui-icons`, and eight `@instructure/ui-*` React packages (consumed only by `renderers/react-markdown`). The entire ingestion blast radius is two files in `@pantoken/core`.

## What's in here

- **Provenance fix** (`@pantoken/tokens`) — records the pinned tag + lockfile commit + ui-icons version instead of the upstream `package.json` version (stuck at `1.0.0` across every tag), exposed at a new `./meta` export.
- **Drift gate** (`tools/upstream-diff`) — a compact committed baseline manifest + a classifier that buckets every upstream change (added/removed/value/syntax/ref tokens; added/removed/**renamed**/changed icons). `vp run upgrade:check` fails on unblessed drift; `vp run upgrade:bless` accepts a reviewed bump. Paths-filtered `upstream-drift` CI job uploads the report.
- **Deprecation lifecycle** (`@pantoken/plugin-deprecations` + `formats/tokens/deprecations.json`) — a dropped token gets a working shim (`var()` forward or frozen value) tracking `deprecatedIn` / `removeIn`. Kept until the removal upstream minor is adopted, then retired + a consumer minor cut. Bless hard-fails to enforce both coverage and retirement.
- **Compatibility manifest** (`compatibility.json` + `docs/compatibility.md`) — a writer/gate pair recording the upstream tiers, validated consumers, and the deprecation table.

## Inaugural v1.4.0→v1.5.0 / 11.7.3→11.7.4 result

77 classified changes: 52 new icons, 1 renamed (`text-select`→`square-dashed-text`), `badge-size` `1.25rem→1rem`, 4 ref retargets, and 2 dropped tokens now shimmed until design-tokens v1.6.0 — `truncate-text-line-height` forwards to `--instui-line-height-paragraph-base` (upstream Truncate v2 inherits line-height), and `badge-notification-z-index` freezes to `1`. Also fixes lucide-react `.js`→`.mjs` ingestion, which the bump broke.

## Verification

`vp run ready` and `vp run check:publish` both green (build, typecheck, all tests, css/js lint, validate-generated, `gate:compatibility`, markdown, publint, attw). `react-markdown` builds and tests against ui-* 11.7.4. Changeset included (minor: model/tokens/plugin-deprecations; patch: core; dependents cascade to patch).

## Future-bump runbook

Bump the catalog pin → `vp install` → rebuild → `vp run upgrade:check` (read the classified report) → author `deprecations.json` entries for removed tokens (or bless refuses) → `vp run upgrade:bless` + `vp run sync:compatibility` → changeset → PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

The release creates ~30 package tags, each fires a `push` event, and there's a well-known GitHub quirk: **`paths` filters are ignored for tag pushes**. So the `push: paths:` trigger runs on every tag → the workflow fires ~30 times per release, doing nothing but `vp --version`.

What it's actually *for*: it's the GitHub Copilot coding agent's environment-setup file (and this repo has `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so Copilot is configured). GitHub invokes the `copilot-setup-steps` job **directly** when provisioning the agent — it doesn't rely on the `on:` triggers at all. The `push`/`pull_request` triggers exist only to validate the file when it changes, and `pull_request` already covers that. So the `push` trigger is both redundant and the sole cause of the spam.

## Problem

`copilot-setup-steps.yml` ran on every release — ~30 times per release, once per package tag — doing nothing but `vp --version`.

## Root cause

The workflow used `push: paths: [.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml]`. GitHub **ignores `paths` filters for tag pushes**, so every package release tag (`@pantoken/…@vX.Y.Z`) matched the `push` trigger regardless of what it changed. Run history confirms it: the runs' `headBranch` values are release tags, not branches.

Drop the `push` trigger. This is safe:

- The GitHub Copilot coding agent runs the `copilot-setup-steps` job **directly** when it provisions its environment — that invocation doesn't depend on the workflow's `on:` triggers, so the file stays fully functional for Copilot.
- The `pull_request` trigger still validates the file whenever it changes, and `workflow_dispatch` still allows manual runs.

No package source changed, so no changeset is needed.

## Problem

`@pantoken/plugin-deprecations@0.2.0` failed to publish on release. It was created as a public package, but a brand-new public `@pantoken/*` package has no npm trusted publisher configured yet, so the OIDC publish fails.

## Fix

It shouldn't be published at all: its deprecation shims are baked into `@pantoken/tokens` at build time, so it's build-time-only tooling (like `@pantoken/upstream-diff` and `@pantoken/validate-generated`), not a consumer package.

- Mark it `private: true` so the release flow skips it.
- Drop the npm-page fields (`publishConfig`, `homepage`, `bugs`, `repository`).
- Keep `exports` and `files` so `@pantoken/tokens` and `@pantoken/upstream-diff` still resolve it in-workspace, and so publint stays clean (`exports` must agree with the packed `files`).

- `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations` builds; `@pantoken/tokens` still resolves the import and bakes the shims (4,639 tokens).

**Why it failed:** I set `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations` up as a public package (modeled on the other plugins), but a brand-new public `@pantoken/*` package has no npm trusted publisher configured, so the OIDC publish fails. And it shouldn't be published anyway — its shims are baked into `@pantoken/tokens` at build time, so it's build-time-only tooling like `@pantoken/upstream-diff` and `@pantoken/validate-generated`.

**Fix:** marked it `private: true` and dropped the npm-page fields (`publishConfig`, `homepage`, `bugs`, `repository`). Kept `exports` + `files` so `@pantoken/tokens` and `@pantoken/upstream-diff` still resolve it in-workspace — and so publint stays clean (it flags `exports` pointing at `dist` when `dist` isn't in `files`).

**Verified:** the plugin still builds, `@pantoken/tokens` still bakes the shims (4,639 tokens), `gate:repository` now checks 68 publishable packages (was 69), publint says "All good!", and `vp run check:publish` is fully green. No changeset needed since it's no longer publishable.

The stale `@pantoken/plugin-deprecations@0.2.0` git tag from the failed release is harmless — nothing published at that version, and future releases will skip the package. Once #42 merges, the release stops trying to publish it.
